10## Abstract
11
12This specification defines an extensible model for managing metadata
13registries. The metadata artifacts can be for any purpose, such as schemas
14or message definitions, and the registry provides both "document" and "API"
15projections of the data to enable their discovery for end-user consumption
16or automation and tooling usage.
17

62## Overview
63
64A Registry consists of two main types of entities: Resources and Groups of
65such Resources.
66
67Resources typically represent the main data of interest in the Registry, while
68Groups, as the name implies, allow related Resources to be arranged together
69under a single collection. Resources can, optionally, also be versioned if
70needed.
71
72This specification defines a set of common metadata that can appear on both
73Resources and Groups, and allows for domain-specific extensions to be added.
74Additionally, this specification defines a common interaction pattern to
75manage, view and discover the entities in the Registry with the goal of
76providing an interoperable framework that will enable common tooling and
77automation.
78
79See the [Registry Design](#registry-design) section for a more complete
80discussion of the xRegistry concepts.
81
82The following 3 diagrams show (from left to right):<br>
831 - The core concepts of the Registry in its most abstract form.<br>
842 - A Registry concept model with multiple types of Groups/Resources.<br>
853 - A concrete sample usage of Registry that includes the use of an attribute
86 on "Message Definition" that is a reference to a "Schema" document - all
87 within the same Registry instance.
88
89<img src="./xregbasicmodel.png"
90 height="300">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<img
91 src="./xregfullmodel.png" height="300">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<img
92 src="./xregsample.png" height="300">
93
94The Registry, while typically exposed as a "service", is also intended to
95support exporting its data as a "document" that can then be used independently
96from the service. For example, the document can be checked into a code
97repository or used as input for tooling. To enable a seamless transition
98between the "document" and "API" views of the data, the specification ensures
99a consistent mapping between the two:
100<img height="250" src="./xregurlmapping.png">
101
102This specification is meant to be a framework from which additional
103specifications can be defined that expose model-specific Resources and
104metadata. See the [Endpoint](./../../endpoint-v1/docs/spec.md) and
105[Schema](./../../schema-v1/docs/spec.md) extension specifications as examples.
106
107Additionally, this specification defines the core model and semantics of
108xRegistry, while secondary specifications (such as
109[xRegistry HTTP Binding](./http.md)) will discuss how to expose them in a
110protocol-specific way.
111
112## Notations and Terminology
113
114### Notational Conventions
115
116The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD",
117"SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be
118interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).
119
120For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are
121OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary.
122Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing
123datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension
124attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported
125or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results
126in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security
127issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.
128
129In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding item is OPTIONAL,
130`*` means the preceding item MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the
131preceding item MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character
132means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in
133the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.
134
135Use of the `<...>` notation indicates a substitutable value that is
136meant to be replaced with a runtime situation-specific value as defined by
137the word/phrase in the angled brackets. For example `<NAME>` would be expected
138to be replaced by the "name" of the item being discussed.
139
140Use of `<GROUP>` and `<RESOURCE>` are meant to represent the singular name of a
141Group and Resource type used, while `<GROUPS>` and `<RESOURCES>` are the plural
142name of those respective types. Use of `<SINGULAR>` represents the singular
143name of the entity referenced. For example, for a "schema document" Resource
144type where its plural name is defined as `schemas` and its singular name is
145defined as `schema`, the `<SINGULAR>` value would be `schema`.
146
147Additionally, the following acronyms are defined:
148- `<GID>` is the `<SINGULAR>id` of a Group.
149- `<RID>` is the `<SINGULAR>id` of a Resource.
150- `<VID>` is the `versionid` of a Version of a Resource.
151
152The following are used to denote an instance of one of the associated data
153types (see [Attributes and Extensions](#attributes-and-extensions) for more
154information about each data type):
155- `<ARRAY>`
156- `<BOOLEAN>`
157- `<DECIMAL>`
158- `<INTEGER>`
159- `<MAP>`
160- `<OBJECT>`
161- `<STRING>`
162- `<TIMESTAMP>`
163- `<UINTEGER>`
164- `<URI>`
165- `<URIABSOLUTE>`
166- `<URIRELATIVE>`
167- `<URITEMPLATE>`
168- `<URL>`
169- `<URLABSOLUTE>`
170- `<URLRELATIVE>`
171- `<XID>`
172- `<XIDTYPE>`
173- `<TYPE>` - one of the allowable data type names (MUST be in lower case)
174 listed in [Attributes and Extensions](#attributes-and-extensions)
175- `<VALUE>` - an instance of one of the above data types
176
177### Terminology
178
179This specification defines the following terms:
180
181#### Aspect
182
183The term "attribute" can be used in many different contexts. In order to avoid
184any potential confusion, "attributes" that are part of an
185[xRegistry model](./model.md) definition are referred to as "aspects" as a
186way to indicate that they are also often mapped to "features" of the
187specification.
188
189#### Group
190
191Groups, as the name implies, allow related Resources to be arranged together
192under a single collection - the Group. The reason for the grouping is not
193defined by this specification, so the owners of the Registry MAY choose to
194define (or enforce) any pattern they wish. In this sense, a Group is similar
195to a "directory" on a filesystem.
196
197An additional common use for Groups is for access control. Managing access
198control on individual Resources, while possible, might be cumbersome, so
199moving it up to the Group could be a more manageable, and user-friendly,
200implementation choice.
201
202#### Registry
203
204A server-side implementation of this specification. Typically, the
205implementation would include model-specific Groups, Resources and extension
206attributes.
207
208There is also a "Registry" entity which acts as the root of an xRegistry
209instance, under which all Groups will reside. The Registry entity itself has
210metadata associated with it.
211
212#### Resource
213
214Resources, typically, represent the main data of interest for the Registry. In
215the filesystem analogy, these would be the "files". Each Resource MUST exist
216under a single Group and, similar to Groups, have a set of Registry metadata.
217However, unlike a Group, which only has Registry metadata, each Resource MAY
218also have a secondary domain-specific "document" associated with it. For
219example, a "schema" Resource might have a "schema document" as its "document".
220This specification places no restriction on the type of content stored in the
221Resource's document. Additionally, Resources (unlike Groups) MAY be versioned.
222
223#### Version
224
225A Version is an instance of a Resource that represents a particular state of
226the Resource. Each Version of a Resource has its own set of xRegistry metadata
227and possibly a domain-specific document associated with it. Each Resource MUST
228have at least one Version associated with it.
229
230Clients MAY interact with specific Versions or with the Resource itself, which
231is equivalent to interacting with the Resource's "default" Version. While in
232many cases the "default" Version will be the "newest" Version, this
233specification allows for the "default" Version to be explicitly chosen and
234unaffected as other Versions are added or removed.
235
236If versioning is not important for the use case in which the Resource is used,
237the sole/default Version can be evolved without creating new ones.
238
239This specification places no requirements on the lifecycle of Versions.
240Implementations, or users of the Registry, determine when new Versions are
241created, as opposed to updating existing Versions, and how many Versions are
242allowed per Resource type.
243
244## Registry Design
245
246As discussed in the [Overview](#overview) section, an xRegistry consists of
247two main entities related to the data being managed: Groups and Resources.
248However, there are other concepts that make up the overall design and this
249section will cover them all in more detail.
250
251Each entity type defined within the Registry will have both a plural and
252singular "type name" associated with it. For example, a Schema Resource
253might have `schemas` as its "plural" type name and `schema` as its "singular"
254type name. This enables the appropriate name to be used based on the context
255in which it appears. In the Schema Resource example, `schemas` would be used
256when a collection of Schemas is referenced, such as in URLs (e.g.
257`.../schemas/myschema`), while `schema` would be used when a single Schema
258is referenced (e.g. as part of its ID name: `schemaid`).
259
260### Design: Registry Entity
261
262An xRegistry instance, or a "Registry", can be thought of as a single rooted
263tree of entities as shown in the "xRegistry Core Spec" diagram in the
264[Overview](#overview) section. At the root is the Registry entity itself.
265This entity is also meant to serve a few other key purposes:
266
267 - Expose high-level metadata about the Registry itself, such as its creation
268 and modified timestamps, name, link to additional documentation, etc.
269 - The set of [capabilities](#registry-capabilities) (features) that are
270 supported. For example, does this Registry support filtering of query
271 results?
272 - The domain-specific ["model"](./model.md#registry-model) that defines the
273 types of entities being managed by the Registry. For example, the model
274 might define a Group called `schemagroups` that has `schemas` as the
275 Resources within those Groups. All xRegistry protocol specifications
276 (e.g. `http`(./http.md) MUST define at least one REQUIRED mechanism by
277 which the model can be retrieved.
278
279### Design: Group Entity
280
281Below the Registry, Groups serve as logical collections of related Resources.
282Each Group exposes the same high-level metadata as the Registry and supports
283user-defined extensions attributes. In practice, Group often act as lightweight
284"directories" for Resources, but they can also encapsulate rich,
285domain-specific data via custom extensions (see [Endpoint](./../../endpoint-v1/docs/spec.md)
286as an example).
287
288### Design: Resource and Version Entities
289
290A Resource entity in the Registry holds one or more Versions of metadata, and
291optionally a domain-specific document. If a Resource holds multiple Versions,
292those can be defined to have [compatibility policies](#compatibility-attribute)
293and [lineage](#ancestorid-attribute). Each Resource always has a default
294Version corresponding to one of the available Versions that is indirectly
295accessed when interacting with the Resource. All held Versions can be accessed
296directly through the Resource's Versions collection.
297
298#### Document Resources vs Metadata-Only Resources
299
300Each Resource MAY be defined to have a "domain-specific" document associated
301with it. These documents MAY be stored within the Registry as an attribute on
302its Versions, or MAY be stored external to the Registry and a URL to its
303location will be stored within the Version instead. This model design choice is
304specified via the
305[`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
306of the Resource type's model definition.
307
308Typically, the domain-specific document will be used when a pre-existing
309document definition already exists and an xRegistry is used as the
310mechanism to expose those documents in a consistent and interoperable way.
311For example, the [Schema Registry](./../../schema-v1/docs/spec.md) only has a few
312xRegistry Resource extension attributes defined because most of the data of
313interest will be in the Schema documents associated with the Resources.
314
315See [Resource Metadata vs Resource
316Document](#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) for more information.
317
318### Design: Registry Views
319
320This specification is designed such that clients can choose how they want the
321data from a server to be returned. There are three main "views" that clients
322can choose from:
323
324#### Single Document View
325
326 In this view, clients retrieving all (or part) of the Registry hierarchy
327 as a single document. In this case, nested (or child) entities MAY be
328 "inlined" into the retrieved document such that the need for secondary
329 interactions with the server is reduced.
330
331 This is often used for cases where the documents are stored in some
332 document storage system (e.g. Github), or as input into local tooling that
333 expects all of the relevant data to be stored locally on disk.
334
335 See the [HTTP `GET /export` operation](./http.md#get-export) for one way to
336 generate this view.
337
338#### API View
339
340 In this view, it is assumed that the client is interested in an interactive
341 discovery and retrieval of the Registry data. Most often clients will "walk"
342 the hierarchy of entities by following the references (links) provided
343 within the serialization of each entity to find the data of interest. As
344 such, in this view, each entity is, by default, retrieved from the server
345 via independent "read" operations.
346
347#### Multiple Document View
348
349 This is a variant of the "API view". In situations where the Registry data
350 is to be stored as independent files either on disk, or in some other object
351 storage system, the client might want to avoid the duplication of
352 information that, by default, a server might generate. For example, they
353 might not want the default Version's metadata to be visible in the owning
354 Resource's serialization.
355
356 Documents generated in this view are often stored locally such that they can
357 be managed independently for use in tooling or stored in some source-code
358 control system (e.g. Github) to minimize the number of conflicting edits
359 between users in a very fluid environment.
360
361 A query with the use of the [Doc flag](#doc-flag), is an example of how to
362 generate this view.
363
364This specification provides the mechanisms to allow for users to choose the
365best "view" for their needs. Regardless of the view, the design allows for
366the retrieved data to then be used as input into an xRegistry server.
367
368### Design: No-Code Servers
369
370One of the goals of xRegistry is to be as broadly supported as possible.
371Requiring all xRegistry endpoints to support the full range of APIs of a
372particular protocol binding might not be feasible in all cases. In particular,
373there might be cases where someone wishes to host a read-only xRegistry server
374and therefore the write operations or advanced features (such as inlining or
375filtering) might not be available. In those cases, simple file serving HTTP
376servers, such as blob stores, ought to be sufficient, and requiring support
377for flag/query parameters and other advanced features (that could require
378custom code) might not always be possible.
379
380To support these simple (no-code) scenarios, this specification (and the
381protocol binding specifications) are written such that the support for the
382various operations and features (e.g. [request flags](#request-flags)) will
383typically be marked as OPTIONAL (often with a "SHOULD" RFC2119 key word).
384However, it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that full servers support as many of the
385operations and features/flags when possible to enable a better user
386experience, and increase interoperability.
387
388See the [HTTP Binding](./http.md#no-code-servers) for more details on how
389this might manifest itself for HTTP servers.
390
391### Design: Protocol Bindings
392
393This specification defines the core model and semantics of an xRegistry
394server implementation without regard to what protocol might be used to
395interact with it.
396
397In general, almost all interactions with a server are OPTIONAL and dictated by
398the specific needs of the environment in which it is being used. However, it is
399STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that servers support the "read" operations, and in
400particular the ability to retrieve the "capabilities" and "model" such that
401tooling can then dynamically discover the remaining data within the Registry.
402
403Implementations MAY choose to incorporate authentication and/or authorization
404mechanisms as needed, but those are out of scope for this specification.
405

407

409Alternative serialization formats MAY be defined.

602 "self": "<URL>", # URL to "meta" object
603 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
604 "xid": "<XID>",
605 "xref": "<XID>", ? # xid of linked Resource
606 "epoch": <UINTEGER>, # Resource's
607 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ? # Resource's
608 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>", # Resource's
609 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>", # Resource's
610 "readonly": <BOOLEAN>, # Default=false
611 "compatibility": "<STRING>", ?
612 "deprecated": {
613 "effective": "<TIMESTAMP>", ?
614 "removal": "<TIMESTAMP>", ?
615 "alternative": "<URL>", ?
616 "documentation": "<URL>"?
617 }, ?
618
619 "defaultversionid": "<STRING>",
620 "defaultversionurl": "<URL>",
621 "defaultversionsticky": <BOOLEAN> ? # Default=false
622 }, ?
623 "versionsurl": "<URL>",
624 "versionscount": <UINTEGER>,
625 "versions": { # Only if inlined
626 "<KEY>": { # The Version's versionid
627 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>", # The Resource's ID
628 "versionid": "<STRING>", # The Version's ID
629 "self": "<URL>", # Version's URL
630 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
631 "xid": "<XID>",
632 "epoch": <UINTEGER>, # Version's epoch
633 "name": "<STRING>", ?
634 "isdefault": <BOOLEAN>, # Default=false
635 "description": "<STRING>", ?
636 "documentation": "<URL>", ?
637 "icon": "<URL>", ?
638 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ? # Version's labels
639 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
640 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
641 "ancestorid": "<STRING>", # Ancestor's versionid
642 "contenttype": "<STRING>", ?
643 "format": "<STRING>", ?
644 "formatvalidated": <BOOLEAN>, ?
645 "formatvalidatedreason": "<STRING>", ?
646 "compatibilityvalidated": <BOOLEAN>, ?
647 "compatibilityvalidatedreason": "<STRING>", ?
648
649 "<RESOURCE>url": "<URL>", ? # If not local
650 "<RESOURCE>": ... Resource document ..., ? # If inlined & JSON
651 "<RESOURCE>base64": "<STRING>" ? # If inlined & ~JSON
652 } *
653 } ?
654 } *
655 } ?
656 } *
657 } ?
658}
659```
660
661If there is an issue with reading or parsing the data provided to the
662server, then an error ([parsing_data](#parsing_data)) MUST be generated.
663
664### Design: Data Retrieval Issues
665
666In general, if a server is unable to retrieve all of the data intended to be
667sent in a response, then an error
668([data_retrieval_error](./spec.md#data_retrieval_error)) MUST be generated and
669the request rejected without any changes being made. However, it is permissible
670for a server to attempt some creative processing. For example, if while
671processing a query the server can only retrieve half of the entities to be
672returned at the current point in time, then it could return those with an
673indication of there being more (via use of a
674[pagination](./../../pagination-v1/docs/spec.md) type of specification). Then during the
675next query request it could return the remainder of the data - or an error if
676it is still not available to retrieve the data. Note that if an entity is to
677be sent, then it MUST be serialized in its entirety (all attributes, and
678requested child entities) or an error MUST be generated.
679
680### Design: Importing Data
681
682There might be situations where someone will do a query to retrieve data
683from a Registry, and then do an update operation to a Registry with that data.
684Depending on the use case, they might not want some of the retrieved data
685to be applied during the update. For example, they might not want the
686`epoch` validation checking to occur. Rather than forcing the user to edit
687the data to remove the potentially problematic attributes, a client MAY use
688the [Ignore Flag](#ignore-flag) to ignore some of the data in the incoming
689request.
690
691### Design: JSON `$schema` keyword
692
693Any JSON xRegistry metadata message that represents a single entity (i.e. not
694a map) MAY include a top-level "$schema" attribute that points to a JSON Schema
695document that describes the message contents. These notations can be used or
696ignored by receivers of these messages. There is no requirement for
697implementations of this specification to persist these values, to include them
698in responses or to use this information.
699
700### Design: Implicit Creation of Parent Entities
701
702To reduce the number of interactions needed when creating an entity, if any of
703its parent entities do not exist, then they MUST be implicitly created. Each of
704those entities MUST be created with the appropriate `<SINGULAR>id` as specified
705by the protocol-specific mechanism by which the nested entity is identified.
706For example, in HTTP the `<PATH>` would include the `<SINGULAR>id` values
707of the parent entities. If any of those entities have REQUIRED attributes,
708then they cannot be implicitly created, and would need to be created directly.
709This also means that the creation of the original entity would fail and
710generate an error
711([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)) for the
712appropriate parent entity.
713
714### Design: Events
715
716xRegistry defines a set of events that SHOULD be generated when changes are
717made to the entities within a Registry. See the [xRegistry Events](./events.md)
718specification for more information.
719
720---
721
722In summary, xRegistry is designed to be a tree of entities that, along with
723its extensible metadata model, can support categorizing, managing and exposing
724a wide range of metadata allowing for a dynamically discoverable, yet
725interoperable, programmatic access via what might otherwise be a
726domain-specific set of APIs.
727
728The following sections will define the technical details of those xRegistry
729entities.
730
731## Registry Model
732
733This section defines the common Registry metadata model, its semantics and
734protocol-independent processing rules. It is an explicit goal for this
735specification that metadata can be created and managed in files in a file
736system, for instance in a Git repository, and also managed in a Registry
737service that implements an xRegistry protocol binding, such as the
738[HTTP Binding](./http.md).
739
740For instance, during development of a module, the metadata about the events
741raised by the modules will best be managed in a file that resides alongside the
742module's source code. When the module is ready to be deployed into a concrete
743system, the metadata about the events will be registered in a Registry service
744along with the endpoints where those events can be subscribed to or consumed
745from, and which allows discovery of the endpoints and all related metadata by
746other systems at runtime.
747
748Therefore, the hierarchical structure of the
749[Registry Model](./model.md#registry-model) is defined in such a way that it
750can be represented in one or more files, including but not limited to JSON, or
751via the entity graph of an API.
752
753In the remainder of this specification, in particular when defining the
754attributes of the Registry entities, the terms "document view" or "API view"
755will be used to indicate whether the serialization of the entity in a response
756is meant for use as a stand-alone document or as part of an API message
757exchange. The most notable differences are that in document view:
758
759- References (e.g. URLs) between entities within responses will use relative
760 references rather than absolute ones. This is an indication to tooling that
761 the entity in question can be found locally and does not need an additional
762 API call to retrieve it.
763- Duplicate data will be removed. In particular, Resources will not include
764 attributes from the "default" Version as part of their serialization. This is
765 done with the assumption the inlined/nested `versions` collection will most
766 likely include the "default" Version, so duplicating that information is
767 redundant.
768
769Most of these differences are to make it easier for tooling to use the
770"stand-alone" document view of the Registry. For a complete list of the
771differences in "document view" see the [Doc Flag](#doc-flag) flag.
772
773Note that "document view" only refers to response messages when the
774[Doc Flag](#doc-flag) is used. There is no "document view" concept for
775requests. However, "document view" responses are designed such that they can
776be used in request messages as they still convey the same information as an
777"API view" response.
778
779Unless otherwise stated in a protocol binding specification, if the processing
780of a request fails (even during the generation of the response) then an error
781MUST be generated and the entire request MUST be undone. See the
782[Error Processing](#error-processing) section for more information.
783
784### Implementation Customizations
785
786This specification does not address many of the details that would need to
787be added for a live instance of a service; as often times these aspects are
788very specific to the environment in which the service is running. For example,
789this specification does not address authentication or authorization levels of
790users, nor how to securely protect the APIs, clients or servers, from attacks.
791Implementations of this specification are expected to add these various
792features as needed.
793
794Additionally, implementations MAY choose to customize the data and behavior on
795a per-user basis as needed. For example, the following non-exhaustive list of
796customizations might be implemented:
797- User-specific capabilities - e.g. admin users might see more features than
798 a non-admin user.
799- User-specific attribute aspects - e.g. admin users might be able to
800 edit a `readonly` Resource. Note that in this case the Resource's `readonly`
801 aspect will likely appear with a value of `true` even for an admin users.
802
803The goal of these customizations is not to allow for implementations to
804violate the specification, rather it is to allow for real-world requirements
805to be met while maintaining the interoperability goals of the specification.
806
807Implementations are encouraged to contact the xRegistry community if it is
808unclear if certain customizations would violate the specification.
809
810Implementations MAY (but are NOT REQUIRED) to validate cross-entity
811constraints that might be violated due to changes in a referenced entity.
812For example, [Endpoint's `envelope`](./../../endpoint-v1/docs/spec.md#envelope) attribute
813mandates that all Messages in that Endpoint use that same `envelope` value.
814One of those Messages might have a `basemessage` value that points to a
815Message that breaks that rule. For a variety of reasons (e.g. authorization
816constraints), server implementations might not be able to verify this
817constraint. Likewise, the same situation might occur via the use of `xref`.
818Clients need to be aware of these possibilities.
819
820### Attributes and Extensions
821
822#### Data Types
823
824Unless otherwise noted, all attributes and extensions MUST be mutable and MUST
825be one of the following data types:
826- `any` - an attribute of this type is one whose type is not known in advance
827 and at runtime MUST be one of the concrete types listed here.
828- `array` - an ordered list of values that are all of the same data type - one
829 of the types listed here.
830 - Some serializations, such as JSON, allow for a `null` value to
831 appear in an array (e.g. `[ null, 2, 3 ]` in an array of integers). In
832 these cases, while it is valid for the serialization being used, it is
833 not valid for xRegistry since `null` is not a valid `integer`. Meaning,
834 the serialization of an array that is syntactically valid for the
835 format being used, but not semantically valid per the
836 [xRegistry model](./model.md#registry-model) definition, MUST NOT be
837 accepted and MUST generate an error
838 ([invalid_attribute](#invalid_attribute)).
839- `boolean` - case-sensitive `true` or `false`.
840- `decimal` - number (integer or floating point).
841- `integer` - signed integer.
842- `map` - set of key/value pairs, where the key MUST be of type string. The
843 value MUST be of one of the types defined here.
844 - Each key MUST:
845 - Be a non-empty string consisting of only lowercase alphanumeric
846 characters (`[a-z0-9]`), `:`, `-`, `_` or a `.`.
847 - Be no longer than 63 characters.
848 - Start with an alphanumeric character.
849 - Be unique within the scope of this map.
850- `object` - a nested entity made up of a set of attributes of these data
851 types.
852- `string` - sequence of Unicode characters.
853- `timestamp` - an [RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) timestamp.
854 Use of a `time-zone` notation is RECOMMENDED. All timestamps returned by
855 a server MUST be normalized to UTC to allow for easy (and consistent)
856 comparisons.
857- `uinteger` - unsigned integer.
858- `uri` - an absolute URI ( `uriabsolute`) or relative URI (`urirelative`).
859- `uriabsolute` - absolute URI as defined in [RFC 3986 Section
860 4.3](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-4.3).
861- `urirelative` - relative URI as defined in [RFC 3986 Section
862 4.2](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-4.2).
863- `uritemplate` - URI Template as defined in
864 [RFC 6570 Section 3.2.1](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6570#section-3.2.1).
865- `url` - an absolute URL (`urlabsolute`) or relative URL (`urlrelative`).
866- `urlabsolute` - an absolute URI as defined in [RFC 3986 Section
867 4.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-4.3) with the
868 added "URL" constraints mentioned in [RFC 3986 Section
869 1.1.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-1.1.3).
870- `urlrelative` - a relative URI as defined in [RFC 3986 Section
871 4.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-4.2) with the
872 added "URL" constraints mentioned in [RFC 3986 Section
873 1.1.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-1.1.3).
874- `xid` - MUST be a case-sensitive URL (xid) reference to another entity
875 defined within the Registry. The actual entity attribute value MAY reference
876 a non-existing entity (i.e. be a dangling pointer), but the syntax MUST
877 reference a defined/valid type in the Registry. This type of attribute is
878 used in place of `url` so that the Registry can do "type checking" to ensure
879 the value references the correct type of Registry entity. See the definition
880 of the [`target` model attribute](./model.md#attributesstringtarget) for more
881 information. Its value MUST start with a `/`.
882- `xidtype` - MUST be a URL reference to an
883 [xRegistry model](./model.md#registry-model) type. The reference MUST point
884 to one of: the Registry itself (`/`), a Group type (`/<GROUPS>`), a
885 Resource type (`/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>`) or Version type for a Resource
886 (`/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>/versions`). Its value MUST reference a
887 defined/valid type in the Registry. It MUST use the plural names of the
888 referenced types, if it is a Group, Resource or Version.
889
890The 6 variants of URI/URL are provided to allow for strict type adherence
891when needed. However, for attributes that are simply "pointers" that might
892in practice be any of those 6 types, it is RECOMMENDED that `uri` be used.
893
894Attributes that are defined to be relative URIs or URLs MUST state what they
895are relative to and any constraints on their values, if any. How, or where,
896this is specified is out of scope of this specification.
897
898The "scalar" data types are:
899 - `boolean`
900 - `decimal`
901 - `integer`
902 - `string`,
903 - `timestamp`
904 - `uinteger`
905 - `uri`
906 - `uriabsolute`
907 - `urirelative`
908 - `uritemplate`,
909 - `url`
910 - `urlabsolute`
911 - `urlrelative`
912 - `xid`
913 - `xidtype`
914
915Note that `any` is not a "scalar" type as its runtime value could be a complex
916type such as `object`.
917
918#### Attributes
919
920All attributes (specification-defined and extensions) MUST adhere to the
921following rules:
922- Their names MUST be between 1 and 63 characters in length.
923- Their names MUST only contain lowercase alphanumeric characters or an
924 underscore (`[a-z0-9_]`) and MUST NOT start with a digit (`[0-9]`).
925- For string attributes, an empty string is a valid value and MUST NOT be
926 treated the same as an attribute with no value (or absence of the attribute).
927- For scalar attributes, the string serialization of the attribute name and
928 its value MUST NOT exceed 4096 bytes. This is to ensure that it can appear
929 in an HTTP header without exceeding implementation limits (see
930 [RFC6265/Limits](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6265#section-6.1)).
931 In cases where larger amounts of data are needed, it is RECOMMENDED that
932 an attribute (of type URL) be defined that references a separate
933 document. For example, `documentation` can be considered such an attribute
934 for `description`.
935- If an attribute's type is not fully defined (i.e. it is defined as an `any`
936 type) but a concrete type is needed to successfully process it, then the
937 server SHOULD default it to type `string`. For example, if an extension is
938 defined as a map whose values are of type `any`, but it appears in an HTTP
939 header with a value of `5` (and it is not clear if this would be an integer
940 or a string), if the server needs to convert this to a concrete data type,
941 then `string` is the default choice.
942- There might be cases when it is not possible to know whether a field name is
943 part of an object (in which case it is an "attribute name"), or is part of
944 a map (in which case it is a "key name"). This decision would impact
945 verification of the field since key names allow for a superset of the
946 characters allowed for attribute names. This will only happen when the
947 `any` type has been used higher-up in the model. As a result, any portion of
948 the entity that appears under the scope of an `any` typed attribute or
949 map-value is NOT REQUIRED to be validated except to ensure that the syntax
950 is valid per the rules of the serialization format used.
951- Attribute instances that have no value (and have no default value defined)
952 are semantically equivalent to having a value of `null` or not being present
953 at all, and for the sake of brevity, SHOULD NOT be serialized as part of its
954 owning entity in server responses. Likewise, specifying them with a value of
955 `null` in client requests SHOULD be reserved for cases where the client
956 needs to indicate a request to delete that attribute value rather than to
957 leave the attribute untouched (absent in the request), such as when `PATCH`
958 is used in the [HTTP Binding Protocol](./http.md).
959- Unless otherwise stated, requests to update read-only attributes MUST be
960 silently ignored by servers, even if the contents of those attributes are
961 invalid.
962- <a id="read-only-changed"></a>Unless otherwise stated, server managed changes
963 to read-only attributes MUST NOT be treated the same as user initiated
964 changes to non-read-only attributes with respect to updating attributes such
965 as `modifiedat` and `epoch`. In other words, as these read-only attributes
966 are changed, the entity MUST NOT be considered "updated".
967
968#### Extensions
969
970Implementations of this specification MAY define additional (extension)
971attributes. However, they MUST adhere to the following rules:
972
973- All extension attributes that appear in the serialization of an entity MUST
974 conform to the model definition of the Registry, otherwise an error
975 ([unknown_attribute](#unknown_attribute)) MUST be generated. This means
976 that they MUST satisfy at least one of the following:
977 - Be explicitly defined (by name) as part of the model.
978 - Be permitted due to the presence of the `*` (undefined) extension attribute
979 name at that level in the model.
980 - Be permitted due to the presence of an `any` type for one of its parent
981 attribute definitions.
982- They MUST NOT conflict with the name of an attribute defined by this
983 specification, including the `<RESOURCE>*` and `<COLLECTION>*` attributes
984 that are implicitly defined. Note that if a Resource type has the
985 [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
986 set the `false` then this rule does not apply for
987 the `<RESOURCE>*` attributes as those attributes are not implicitly defined
988 for that Resource type.
989- It is RECOMMENDED that extension attributes on different entities do not
990 use the same name unless they have the exact same semantic meaning.
991- It is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that they be named in such a way as to avoid
992 potential conflicts with future xRegistry specification-defined attributes.
993 For example, use of a model (or domain) specific prefix could be used to help
994 avoid possible future conflicts.
995
996Use of an attribute (specification defined, or extension) that does not
997conform to this specification MUST generate an error
998([invalid_attribute](#invalid_attribute)).
999
1000#### Common Attributes
1001
1002The following attributes are used by one or more entities defined by this
1003specification. They are defined here once rather than repeating them throughout
1004the specification.
1005
1006For easy reference, the JSON serialization of these attributes MUST adhere to
1007this form:
1008- `"<SINGULAR>id": "<STRING>"`
1009- `"self": "<URL>"`
1010- `"shortself": "<URL>"`
1011- `"xid": "<XID>"`
1012- `"epoch": <UINTEGER>`
1013- `"name": "<STRING>"`
1014- `"description": "<STRING>"`
1015- `"documentation": "<URL>"`
1016- `"icon": "<URL>"`
1017- `"labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }`
1018- `"createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>"`
1019- `"modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>"`
1020- `"deprecated": "<OBJECT>"`
1021
1022The definition of each attribute is defined below:
1023
1024##### `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute
1025
1026- Type: String
1027- Description: An immutable unique identifier of the owning entity.
1028 The actual name of this attribute will vary based on the model entity it
1029 identifies. For example, a `schema` Resource would use an attribute name
1030 of `schemaid`. This attribute MUST be named `registryid` for the Registry
1031 itself, and MUST be named `versionid` for all Version entities.
1032
1033- Constraints:
1034 - REQUIRED.
1035 - MUST be immutable.
1036 - MUST be a non-empty string consisting of [RFC3986 `unreserved`
1037 characters](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-2.3)
1038 (ALPHA / DIGIT / `-` / `.` / `_` / `~`), `:` or `@`, MUST start with
1039 ALPHA, DIGIT or `_` and MUST be between 1 and 128 characters in length.
1040 Otherwise, an error ([malformed_id](#malformed_id)) MUST be generated.
1041 - MUST be unique (case-insensitively) within the scope of the entity's
1042 parent.
1043 - This attribute MUST be treated as case-sensitive for look-up purposes.
1044 For example, an HTTP request URL to an entity with the wrong case for its
1045 `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be treated as "not found".
1046 - In cases where an entity's `<SINGULAR>id` is specified outside of the
1047 serialization of the entity (e.g. part of a request URL, or a map key),
1048 its presence within the serialization of the entity is OPTIONAL. However,
1049 if present, it MUST be the same as any other specification of the
1050 `<SINGULAR>id` outside of the entity, and it MUST be the same as the
1051 entity's existing `<SINGULAR>id` if one exists, otherwise an error
1052 ([mismatched_id](#mismatched_id)) MUST be generated.
1053
1054- Examples:
1055 - `a183e0a9-abf8-4763-99bc-e6b7fcc9544b`
1056 - `myEntity`
1057 - `myEntity.example.com`
1058
1059While `<SINGULAR>id` can be something like a UUID, when possible, it is
1060RECOMMENDED that it be human friendly as these values will often appear in
1061user-facing situations such as URLs or as command-line parameters.
1062Additionally, In cases where [`name`](#name-attribute) is absent, the
1063`<SINGULAR>id` might be used as the display name.
1064
1065Note, since `<SINGULAR>id` is immutable, in order to change its value, a new
1066entity would need to be created with the new `<SINGULAR>id` that is a deep-copy
1067of the existing entity. Then the existing entity would be deleted.
1068
1069##### `self` Attribute
1070
1071- Type: URL
1072- Description: A server-generated unique URL referencing the current entity.
1073 - Each entity in the Registry MUST have a unique `self` URL value that
1074 locates the entity in the Registry hierarchy and from where the entity can
1075 be retrieved.
1076 - When specified as an absolute URL, it MUST be based on the URL of the
1077 Registry root appended with the hierarchy path of the Registry
1078 entities/collections leading to the entity (its `xid` value).
1079 - When specified as a relative URL, it MUST end with the entity's `xid`
1080 value.
1081
1082- API View Constraints:
1083 - REQUIRED.
1084 - MUST be immutable.
1085 - MUST be a non-empty absolute URL based on the URL of the Registry.
1086 - When serializing Resources or Versions, whose Resource type's
1087 [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
1088 is set to `true`, then (based on the protocol binding being used) this
1089 attribute might need to include some indicator that the xRegistry metadata
1090 is to be returned rather than the domain-specific document. See the
1091 [Resource Metadata vs Resource
1092 Document](./http.md#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) section for how
1093 this might manifest itself for HTTP.
1094 - MUST be a read-only attribute.
1095
1096- Document View Constraints:
1097 - REQUIRED.
1098 - MUST be immutable.
1099 - MUST be a relative URL of the form `#JSON-POINTER` where the `JSON-POINTER`
1100 locates this entity within the current document. See [Doc Flag](#doc-flag)
1101 for more information.
1102 - This URL MUST NOT include any indicator signifying the entity's xRegistry
1103 metadata rather than its domain-specific document (e.g. `$details` in the
1104 [HTTP binding](./http.md) case).
1105
1106- Examples:
1107 - `https://example.com/registry/schemagroups/g1/schemas/s1$details` (API View)
1108 - `https://example.com/registry/endpoints/ep1` (API View)
1109 - `#/endpoints/ep1` (Document View)
1110
1111##### `shortself` Attribute
1112
1113- Type: URL
1114- Description: A server-generated unique absolute URL for an entity. This
1115 attribute MUST be an alternative URL for the entity's `self`
1116 (non-`$details` suffixed) URL. When a client constructs a request based on
1117 the `shortself` URL, it MAY append `$details`, or any flags (e.g. query
1118 parameters), that are valid for use on the `self` URL.
1119
1120 The intention is that `shortself` SHOULD be shorter in length
1121 than `self` such that it MAY be used when the length of the URL referencing
1122 the entity is important. For example, in cases where the size of a
1123 message referencing this entity needs to be as small as possible.
1124
1125 This specification makes no statement as to how this URL is constructed,
1126 to which host/path it references, or whether a request to this URL
1127 will directly perform the desired operation or whether it returns a
1128 redirect to the full `self` URL requiring the client to resend the request.
1129
1130 If an entity is deleted and then a new entity is created that results in
1131 the same `self` URL, this specification does not mandate that the same
1132 `shortself` be generated, but it MAY do so.
1133
1134 This attribute MUST only appear in the serialization if the `shortself`
1135 capability is enabled. However, if this capability is enabled, then disabled,
1136 and then re-enabled, the `shortself` values MUST retain their original
1137 values. In this sense, implementations might create a `shortself` that is
1138 known for the lifetime of the entity and the capability controls whether
1139 the attribute is serialized or not.
1140
1141 When the `shortself` capability is disabled, the attribute name `shortself`
1142 is still a reserved attribute name and MUST NOT be used as an extension.
1143
1144- Constraints:
1145 - REQUIRED if the `shortself` capability is enabled.
1146 - MUST NOT appear in responses if the `shortself` capability is disabled.
1147 - MUST be immutable for the lifetime of the entity.
1148 - MUST be unique across all entities in the Registry.
1149 - MUST be a non-empty absolute URL referencing the same entity as the `self`
1150 URL, either directly or indirectly via a protocol-specific redirect.
1151 - MUST be a read-only attribute.
1152 - MUST NOT contain the `$` character as that is reserved for specification
1153 defined suffixes (such as `$details`).
1154
1155- Examples:
1156 - `https://tinyurl.com/xreg123` redirects to
1157 `https://example.com/endpoints/e1`
1158
1159##### `xid` Attribute
1160
1161- Type: XID
1162- Description: An immutable server-generated unique identifier of the entity.
1163 Unlike `<SINGULAR>id`, which is unique within the scope of its parent, `xid`
1164 MUST be unique across the entire Registry, and as such is defined to be a
1165 relative URL from the root of the Registry. This value MUST be the same as
1166 the `<PATH>` portion of its `self` URL, after the Registry's base URL,
1167 without any protocol-specific xRegistry suffix (e.g. `$details` in the HTTP
1168 case). Unlike some other relative URIs, `xid` values MUST NOT be shortened
1169 based on the incoming request's URL; `xid`s are always relative to the root
1170 path of the Registry.
1171
1172 This attribute is provided as a convenience for users who need a reference
1173 to the entity without running the risk of incorrectly extracting it from
1174 the `self` URL, which might be ambiguous at times. The `xid` value is also
1175 meant to be used as an `xref` value (see [Cross Referencing
1176 Resources](#cross-referencing-resources), or as the value for attributes of
1177 type `xid` (see [`target` model
1178 attribute](./model.md#attributesstringtarget)).
1179
1180- Constraints:
1181 - REQUIRED.
1182 - MUST be immutable.
1183 - MUST be a case-sensitive non-empty relative URL to the current entity.
1184 - MUST be of the form:
1185 `/[<GROUPS>/<GID>[/<RESOURCES>/<RID>[/meta | /versions/<VID>]]]` and
1186 reference valid Group and Resource types. Otherwise, an error
1187 ([malformed_xid](#malformed_xid)) MUST be generated.
1188 - MUST start with the `/` character.
1189 - MUST be a read-only attribute.
1190
1191- Examples:
1192 - `/endpoints/ep1`
1193 - `/schemagroups/myschemas/schemas/app.json/versions/v1.0`
1194
1195##### `epoch` Attribute
1196
1197- Type: Unsigned Integer
1198- Description: A numeric value used to determine whether an entity has been
1199 modified. Each time the associated entity is updated, this value MUST be
1200 set to a new value that is greater than the current one. This attribute
1201 MUST be updated for every update operation, even if no attributes were
1202 explicitly updated, such as a "patch" type of operation when no attributes
1203 are specified. This then acts like a `touch` type of operation.
1204
1205 During a single write operation, whether this value is incremented for
1206 each modified attribute of the entity, or updated just once for the entire
1207 operation is an implementation choice.
1208
1209 During a create operation, if this attribute is present in the request, then
1210 it MUST be silently ignored by the server.
1211
1212 During an update, or delete, operation, if this attribute is present in the
1213 request, then an error
1214 ([mismatched_epoch](#mismatched_epoch)) MUST be generated if the
1215 request includes a non-null value that differs from the existing value.
1216 This allows for the detection of concurrent, but conflicting, updates to the
1217 same entity to be detected. A value of `null` MUST be treated the same as a
1218 request with no `epoch` attribute at all, in which case a check MUST NOT
1219 be performed.
1220
1221 If an entity has a nested xRegistry collection, its `epoch` value MUST
1222 be updated each time an entity in that collection is added or removed.
1223 However, its `epoch` value MUST NOT be updated solely due to modifications of
1224 an existing entity in the collection.
1225
1226 Note that Resource entities have an `epoch` value that is serialized
1227 as part of its [`meta` entity](#meta-entity). Its value is only incremented
1228 when the `meta` attributes are updated, or when a Version is added, or
1229 removed, from that Resource.
1230
1231- Constraints:
1232 - REQUIRED.
1233 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.
1234 - MUST be an unsigned integer equal to or greater than zero.
1235 - MUST increase in value each time the entity is updated.
1236
1237- Examples:
1238 - `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`
1239
1240##### `name` Attribute
1241
1242- Type: String
1243- Description: A human-readable name of the entity. This is often used
1244 as the "display name" for an entity rather than the `<SINGULAR>id` especially
1245 when the `<SINGULAR>id` might be something that isn't human friendly, like a
1246 UUID. In cases where `name` is absent, the `<SINGULAR>id` value SHOULD be
1247 displayed in its place.
1248
1249 This specification places no uniqueness constraints on this attribute.
1250 This means that two sibling entities MAY have the same value. Therefore,
1251 this value MUST NOT be used for unique identification purposes, the
1252 `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be used instead.
1253
1254 Note that implementations MAY choose to enforce additional constraints on
1255 this value. For example, they could mandate that `<SINGULAR>id` and `name` be
1256 the same value. Or, it could mandate that `name` be unique within the scope
1257 of a parent entity. How any such requirement is shared with all parties is
1258 out of scope of this specification.
1259
1260- Constraints:
1261 - OPTIONAL.
1262 - If present, MUST be non-empty.
1263
1264- Examples:
1265 - `My Cool Endpoint`
1266
1267##### `description` Attribute
1268
1269- Type: String
1270- Description: A human-readable summary of the purpose of the entity.
1271
1272- Constraints:
1273 - OPTIONAL.
1274
1275- Examples:
1276 - `A queue of the sensor-generated messages`
1277
1278##### `documentation` Attribute
1279
1280- Type: URL
1281- Description: A URL to additional information about this entity.
1282 This specification does not place any constraints on the data returned from
1283 a query to this URL.
1284
1285- Constraints:
1286 - OPTIONAL.
1287 - If present, MUST be a non-empty URL.
1288 - MUST support retrieving the information via a query to this URL.
1289
1290- Examples:
1291 - `https://example.com/docs/myQueue`
1292
1293##### `icon` Attribute
1294
1295- Type: URL
1296- Description: A URL to a graphical icon for the entity.
1297
1298- Constraints:
1299 - OPTIONAL.
1300 - If present, MUST be a non-empty URL.
1301 - MUST be retrievable via a query to this URL.
1302 - STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that the icon be in SVG or PNG format and square.
1303
1304- Examples:
1305 - `https://example.com/myRegistry.svg`
1306
1307##### `labels` Attribute
1308
1309- Type: Map of name/value string pairs
1310- Description: A mechanism in which additional metadata about the entity can
1311 be stored without changing the model definition of the entity.
1312
1313- Constraints:
1314 - OPTIONAL.
1315 - If present, MUST be a map of zero or more name/value string pairs. See
1316 [Attributes and Extensions](#attributes-and-extensions) for more
1317 information.
1318 - Keys MUST be non-empty strings.
1319 - Values MAY be empty strings.
1320
1321- Examples:
1322 - `"labels": { "owner": "John", "verified": "" }`
1323
1324##### `createdat` Attribute
1325
1326- Type: Timestamp
1327- Description: The date/time of when the entity was created.
1328
1329- Constraints:
1330 - REQUIRED.
1331 - MUST be a [RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) timestamp.
1332 - This specification places no restrictions on the value of this attribute,
1333 nor on its value relative to its `modifiedat` value or the current
1334 date/time. Implementations MAY choose to restrict its values if necessary.
1335 - If present in a write operation request, the value MUST override any
1336 existing value, however a value of `null` MUST use the current date/time
1337 as the new value.
1338 - When absent in an update request, any existing value MUST remain
1339 unchanged.
1340 - During the processing of a single request, all entities that have their
1341 `createdat` or `modifiedat` attributes set to the current date/time MUST
1342 use the same value in all cases.
1343
1344- Examples:
1345 - `2030-12-19T06:00:00Z`
1346
1347##### `modifiedat` Attribute
1348
1349- Type: Timestamp
1350- Description: The date/time of when the entity was last updated.
1351
1352- Constraints:
1353 - REQUIRED.
1354 - MUST be a [RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) timestamp
1355 representing the time when the entity was last updated.
1356 - This specification places no restrictions on the value of this attribute,
1357 nor on its value relative to its `createdat` value or the current
1358 date/time. Implementations MAY choose to restrict its values if necessary.
1359 - Any update operation (even one that does not change any attribute, MUST
1360 update this attribute. This then acts like a `touch` type of operation.
1361 - Updates to an existing entity in an xRegistry collection MUST NOT cause an
1362 update to its parent entity's `modifiedat` value. However, adding or
1363 removing an entity from a nested xRegistry collection MUST update the
1364 `modifiedat` value of the parent entity.
1365 - If present in a write operation request, the following applies:
1366 - If the request value is `null` or the same as the existing value, then
1367 the current date/time MUST be used as its new value.
1368 - If the request value is different than the existing value, then the
1369 request value MUST be used as its new value.
1370 - When absent in a write operation request, it MUST be set to the current
1371 date/time.
1372 - During the processing of a single request, all entities that have their
1373 `createdat` or `modifiedat` attributes set to the current date/time MUST
1374 use the same value in all cases.
1375
1376- Examples:
1377 - `2030-12-19T06:00:00Z`
1378
1379##### `deprecated` Attribute
1380
1381- Type: Object containing the following properties:
1382 - `effective`<br>
1383 An OPTIONAL property indicating the time when the entity entered, or will
1384 enter, a deprecated state. The date MAY be in the past or future. If this
1385 property is not present the entity is already in a deprecated state.
1386 If present, this MUST be an [RFC3339][rfc3339] timestamp.
1387
1388 - `removal`<br>
1389 An OPTIONAL property indicating the time when the entity MAY be removed.
1390 The entity MUST NOT be removed before this time. If this property is not
1391 present, the client cannot make any assumptions as to when the entity
1392 might be removed. Note: as with most properties, this property is mutable.
1393 If present, this MUST be an [RFC3339][rfc3339] timestamp and MUST NOT be
1394 sooner than the `effective` time if present.
1395
1396 - `alternative`<br>
1397 An OPTIONAL property specifying the URL to an alternative entity the
1398 client can consider as a replacement for this entity. There is no
1399 guarantee that the referenced entity is an exact replacement, rather the
1400 client is expected to investigate the entity to determine if it is
1401 appropriate.
1402
1403 - `documentation`<br>
1404 An OPTIONAL property specifying the URL to additional information about
1405 the deprecation of the entity. This specification does not mandate any
1406 particular format or information, however some possibilities include:
1407 reasons for the deprecation or additional information about likely
1408 alternative entities. The URL MUST support retrieval of the information
1409 via a query.
1410
1411 Note that an implementation is not mandated to use this attribute in
1412 advance of removing an entity, but it is RECOMMENDED to do so.
1413
1414 This attribute can appear on Groups and Resources, however, this
1415 specification makes no statement as to the relationship, or validity, of the
1416 values of each with respect to how they might impact each other.
1417
1418- Constraints:
1419 - OPTIONAL
1420- Examples:
1421 - `"deprecated": {}`
1422 - ```
1423 "deprecated": {
1424 "removal": "2030-12-19T00:00:00Z",
1425 "alternative": "https://example.com/entities-v2/myentity"
1426 }
1427 ```
1428
1429##### `constraints` Attribute
1430
1431- Type: Map of Resource attributes to be constrained just for this Group.
1432
1433 This attribute is used to create a set of Group instance specific constraints
1434 on the Resources that exist within it. For example, with this mechanism a
1435 Group can restrict all Resources within it to only have a subset of the
1436 allowed values for a particular attribute. This allows for Group instance
1437 specific restrictions without requiring the creating of new Resource types.
1438
1439 These restrictions are designed to only allow subsetting of the definitions
1440 specified by the Resource type model and any Group type model
1441 [`constraints`](./model.md#groupsstringconstraints) defined. They MUST NOT be
1442 used to extend the allowable values of the attributes being constrained.
1443
1444 The definition of this map is the same as the model Group type
1445 [`constraints`](./model.md#groupsstringconstraints) attribute.
1446
1447 Any map key value specified here that is the same as a key value included
1448 in the Group type model's [`constraints`](./model.md#groupsstringconstraints),
1449 is interpreted as a request to further constrain the Resource attribute
1450 being referenced.
1451
1452 The two layers of definitions of the constraints are merged such that any
1453 individual constraint aspect defined at the Group instance level MUST
1454 only further restrict any constraint aspect mentioned at the Group type
1455 level. Absence of (or `null` value for) an aspect at the Group instance
1456 level MUST NOT impact any constraints defined at the Group type level.
1457
1458 The following further clarifies this merging:
1459 - If `enum` is specified at both levels, then the Group instance `enum` set
1460 MUST be a subset of the `enum` defined at the Group type level.
1461 - If the `equals` aspect is defined in both levels then they MUST be the
1462 exact same value. And in that situation, specifying it at the Group
1463 instance level is redundant. For clarity, a Group instance MAY introduce
1464 an `equals` aspect for a constraint key defined at the model Group type
1465 level that has no `equals` aspect.
1466
1467- Constraints:
1468 - OPTIONAL
1469- Examples:
1470 ```yaml
1471 "constraints": {
1472 "schemas.format" : {
1473 "default": "jsonschema/draft-07",
1474 "enum": [ "avro/1.9", "jsonschema/draft-07" ],
1475 "equals": "format"
1476 }
1477 }
1478 ```
1479 The above example mandates that:
1480 - All schema Resources within this group have a `format` values that
1481 is either `avro/1.9` or `jsonschema/draft-07`. And when not specified,
1482 it will default to `jsonschema/draft-07`.
1483 - It also ensures that each Resource's `format` attribute is the same as
1484 the owning Group's `format` values (if present).
1485
1486### Registry Collections
1487
1488Registry collections (`<GROUPS>`, `<RESOURCES>` and `versions`) that are
1489defined by the [Registry Model](./model.md#registry-model) MUST be serialized
1490according to the rules defined in this section.
1491
1492The serialization of a collection is done as 3 attributes and they MUST adhere
1493to their respective forms as follows:
1494
1495```yaml
1496"<COLLECTION>url": "<URL>",
1497"<COLLECTION>count": <UINTEGER>,
1498"<COLLECTION>": {
1499 # Map of entities in the collection, key is the "<SINGULAR>id" of the entity
1500}
1501```
1502
1503Where:
1504- The term `<COLLECTION>` MUST be the plural name of the collection
1505 (e.g. `endpoints`, `versions`).
1506- The `<COLLECTION>url` attribute MUST be a URL that can be used to retrieve
1507 the `<COLLECTION>` map via a protocol-specific query mechanism. This URL
1508 MAY include any necessary [filtering](#filter-flag) and MUST be a
1509 read-only attribute. This attribute MUST be an absolute URL except in
1510 document view when the collection is inlined, in which case it MUST be a
1511 relative URL.
1512- The `<COLLECTION>count` attribute MUST contain the number of entities in the
1513 `<COLLECTION>` map (after any necessary [filtering](#filter-flag)) and MUST
1514 be a read-only attribute.
1515- The `<COLLECTION>` attribute is a map and MUST contain the entities of the
1516 collection (after any necessary [filtering](#filter-flag)), and MUST use
1517 the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity as its map key.
1518- The key of each entity in the collection map MUST be unique within the scope
1519 of the collection.
1520- The specifics of whether each `<COLLECTION>*` attribute is REQUIRED or
1521 OPTIONAL will be based on whether the document- or API-view is used. See
1522 the next section for more information.
1523
1524When the `<COLLECTION>` attribute is expected to be present in the
1525serialization, but the number of entities in the collection is zero, it MUST
1526still be included as an empty map (e.g. `{}`) in the serialization.
1527
1528The set of entities that are part of the `<COLLECTION>` attribute is a
1529point-in-time view of the Registry. There is no guarantee that a future query
1530to the `<COLLECTION>url` will return the exact same collection since the
1531contents of the Registry might have changed. This specification makes no
1532statement as to whether a subsequent query that is missing previously returned
1533entities is an indication of those entities being deleted or not.
1534
1535**Examples:**
1536
1537Sample `schemagroups` collection attributes, with `schemagroups` inlined.
1538
1539```yaml
1540"schemagroupsurl": "http://registry.example.com/schemagroups",
1541"schemagroupscount": 8
1542"schemagroups": {
1543 "Contoso.ERP": {...},
1544 "Fabrikam.InkJetPrinter": {...},
1545 "Fabrikam.Lumen": {...},
1546 "Fabrikam.RoboVac": {...},
1547 "Fabrikam.SmartOven": {...},
1548 "Fabrikam.Watchkam": {...},
1549 "WaterBoiler": {...},
1550 "WindGenerator": {...}
1551},
1552```
1553
1554The requirements on the presence of the 3 `<COLLECTION>*` attributes varies
1555between document and API views, and is defined below:
1556
1557#### Collections in Document View
1558
1559In document view:
1560- `<COLLECTION>url` and `<COLLECTION>count` are OPTIONAL.
1561- `<COLLECTION>` is conditional in responses based on the values in the
1562 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag). If a collection is part of the flag's value then
1563 `<COLLECTION>` MUST be present in the response even if it is empty
1564 (e.g. `{}`). If the collection is not part of the flag value then
1565 `<COLLECTION>` MUST NOT be included in the response.
1566
1567#### Collections in API View
1568
1569In API view:
1570- `<COLLECTION>url` is REQUIRED for responses even if there are no entities
1571 in the collection.
1572- `<COLLECTION>count` is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED for responses even if
1573 there are no entities in the collection. This requirement is not mandated
1574 to allow for cases where calculating the exact count is too costly.
1575- `<COLLECTION>url` and `<COLLECTION>count` are OPTIONAL in requests and MUST
1576 be silently ignored by the server if present.
1577- `<COLLECTION>` is conditional in responses based on the values in the
1578 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag). If a collection is part of the flag's value then
1579 `<COLLECTION>` MUST be present in the response even if it is empty
1580 (e.g. `{}`). If the collection is not part of the flag value then
1581 `<COLLECTION>` MUST NOT be included in the response.
1582- `<COLLECTION>` is OPTIONAL for requests. See [Updating Nested Registry
1583 Collections](#updating-nested-registry-collections) for more details.
1584
1585#### Updating Nested Registry Collections
1586
1587When updating an entity that can contain xRegistry collections, the request
1588MAY contain the 3 collection attributes. The `<COLLECTION>url` and
1589`<COLLECTION>count` attributes MUST be silently ignored by the server.
1590
1591If the `<COLLECTION>` attribute is present, the server MUST process each entity
1592in the collection map as a request to create or update that entity according to
1593the semantics of the operation method used. An entry in the map that isn't a
1594valid entity (e.g. is `null`) MUST generate an error
1595([bad_request](#bad_request)).
1596
1597For example, in the case of HTTP:
1598
1599```yaml
1600PUT https://example.com/endpoints/ep1
1601
1602{
1603 "endpointid": "ep1",
1604 "name": "A cool endpoint",
1605
1606 "messages": {
1607 "mymsg1": { ... },
1608 "mymsg2:" { ... }
1609 }
1610}
1611```
1612
1613will not only create/update an `endpoint` Group with an `endpointid` of `ep1`
1614but will also create/update its `message` Resources (`mymsg1` and `mymsg2`).
1615
1616Any error while processing a nested collection entity MUST result in the entire
1617request being rejected.
1618
1619An absent `<COLLECTION>` attribute, or empty map, MUST be interpreted as a
1620request to not modify the collection at all.
1621
1622If a client wishes to delete an entity from the collection, or replace the
1623entire collection, the client MUST use a "delete" type of operations on the
1624collection. This means that delete operations on these entities would need
1625to be handled in dedicated operations, separate from update operations.
1626
1627In cases where a Resource update operation includes attributes meant to be
1628applied to the "default" Version of a Resource, and the incoming inlined
1629`versions` collections includes that "default" Version, the Resource's default
1630Version attributes MUST be silently ignored. This is to avoid any possible
1631conflicting data between the two sets of data for that Version. In other
1632words, the Version attributes in the incoming `versions` collection wins.
1633See [Resource Processing Algorithm](#resource-processing-algorithm) for more
1634details.
1635
1636To better understand this scenario, consider the following HTTP request to
1637update a Message where the `defaultversionid` is `v1`:
1638
1639```yaml
1640PUT http://example.com/endpoints/ep1/messages/msg1
1641
1642{
1643 "messageid": "msg1",
1644 "versionid": "v1",
1645 "name": "Blob Created"
1646
1647 "versions": {
1648 "v1": {
1649 "messageid": "msg1",
1650 "versionid": "v1",
1651 "name": "Blob Created Message Definition"
1652 }
1653 }
1654}
1655```
1656
1657If the `versions` collection were not present with the `v1` entity then the
1658top-level attributes would be used to update the default Version (`v1` in this
1659case). However, because it is present, the request to update `v1` becomes
1660ambiguous because it is not clear if the server is meant to use the top-level
1661attributes or if it is to use the attributes under the `v1` entity of the
1662`versions` collection. When both sets of attributes are the same, then it does
1663not matter. However, in this example, the `name` attributes have different
1664values. The paragraph above mandates that in these potentially ambiguous cases
1665the entity in the `versions` collection is to be used and the top-level
1666attributes are to be ignored. So, in this case the `name` of the default (`v1`)
1667Version will be `Blob Created Message Definition`.
1668
1669### Registry Entity
1670
1671The Registry entity represents the root of a Registry and is the main
1672entry-point for traversal and discovery.
1673
1674The serialization of the Registry entity MUST adhere to this form:
1675
1676```yaml
1677{
1678 "specversion": "<STRING>",
1679 "registryid": "<STRING>",
1680 "self": "<URL>",
1681 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
1682 "xid": "<XID>",
1683 "epoch": <UINTEGER>,
1684 "name": "<STRING>", ?
1685 "description": "<STRING>", ?
1686 "documentation": "<URL>", ?
1687 "icon": "<URL>", ?
1688 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ?
1689 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
1690 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
1691
1692 "capabilities": { Registry capabilities }, ? # Only if inlined
1693 "model": { Registry model }, ? # Only if inlined
1694 "modelsource": { Registry model }, ? # Only if inlined
1695
1696 # Repeat for each Group type
1697 "<GROUPS>url": "<URL>", # e.g. "endpointsurl"
1698 "<GROUPS>count": <UINTEGER>, # e.g. "endpointscount"
1699 "<GROUPS>": { Groups collection } ? # Only if inlined
1700}
1701```
1702
1703This entity behaves like all other entities in the Registry with respect to
1704how it is managed. However, since it contains attributes that are only visible
1705upon request (e.g. `model` and `capabilities`), for clarity, when those
1706attributes are modified the Registry entity is considered to be updated, and
1707therefore its `epoch` and `modifiedat` values MUST be updated per their
1708defined semantics.
1709
1710The Registry entity includes the following
1711[common attributes](#common-attributes):
1712- [`registryid`](#singularid-id-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document
1713 views. OPTIONAL in requests.
1714- [`self`](#self-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
1715 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
1716- [`shortself`](#shortself-attribute) - OPTIONAL in API and document views,
1717 based on the `shortself` capability. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
1718- [`xid`](#xid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
1719 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
1720- [`epoch`](#epoch-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL
1721 in requests.
1722- [`name`](#name-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
1723- [`description`](#description-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
1724- [`documentation`](#documentation-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
1725- [`icon`](#icon-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
1726- [`labels`](#labels-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
1727- [`createdat`](#createdat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
1728 OPTIONAL in requests.
1729- [`modifiedat`](#modifiedat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
1730 OPTIONAL in requests.
1731
1732and the following Registry-level attributes:
1733
1734#### `specversion` Attribute
1735- Type: String.
1736- Description: The version of this specification that the document
1737 adheres to.
1738
1739- Constraints:
1740 - REQUIRED.
1741 - MUST be a read-only attribute.
1742 - MUST be non-empty.
1743
1744- Examples:
1745 - `1.0`
1746
1747#### `capabilities` Attribute
1748- Type: [Registry Capabilities](#registry-capabilities)
1749- Description: The set of capabilities (features) supported by the Registry.
1750 See [Registry Capabilities](#registry-capabilities) for more information.
1751
1752 During a write operation:
1753 - The absence of this attribute MUST result in no changes to the capabilities
1754 of the Registry.
1755 - An explicit value of `null` for this attribute MUST result in resetting the
1756 capabilities to the server's default values.
1757 - If present, MUST be processed before any other attributes since subsequent
1758 processing might be impacted by the new capability values. In cases where
1759 a capability setting influences the processing of this attribute, or
1760 of the [`modelsource`](#modelsource-attribute), the state of those
1761 particular settings prior to the request MUST be used for the duration
1762 of the current request. For example:
1763 - Support for `ignore=capabilities` would be controlled by
1764 the pre-request configuration since, if set, would result in ignoring
1765 any `capabilities` attribute in the request.
1766 - However, the set of supported `formats` would be controlled by the
1767 updated `capabilities` to ensure proper validation of the Registry data
1768 prior to completing the request.
1769
1770- Constraints:
1771 - MUST NOT be included in API and document views unless requested via the
1772 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
1773 - MUST be included in API and document views if requested via the
1774 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
1775 - MAY be mutable based on the capabilities of the implementation.
1776
1777#### `model` Attribute
1778- Type: [Registry Model](./model.md#registry-model).
1779- Description: A full description of the Groups, Resources and attributes
1780 (specification-defined and extensions) as defined by the current model
1781 associated with this Registry. See
1782 [Registry Model](./model.md#registry-model).
1783
1784 This view of the model is useful for tooling that needs a complete view of
1785 what will be part of any message exchange with the server.
1786
1787- Constraints:
1788 - MUST NOT be included in API and document views unless requested via the
1789 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
1790 - MUST be included in API and document views if requested via the
1791 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
1792 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.
1793
1794#### `modelsource` Attribute
1795- Type: [Registry Model](./model.md#registry-model).
1796- Description: The "model" definition that was last used to define this
1797 Registry's model. Unlike `model`, which includes all aspects of the model,
1798 this is meant to represent just the customizations, or extensions, to the
1799 base [xRegistry model](./model.md#registry-model) as defined in this
1800 specification. This allows for users to view (and edit) just the custom
1801 aspects of the model without the "noise" of the specification-defined parts.
1802
1803 During a write operation:
1804 - The absence of this attribute MUST result in no changes to the model, or
1805 modelsource of the Registry.
1806 - An explicit value of `null`, or an empty JSON object (`{}`), MUST result
1807 in all Groups, Resources and extension Registry-level attributes being
1808 removed from the model.
1809 - If present, the Registry's model MUST be updated prior to any entities
1810 being updated, including the other Registry-level attributes. However,
1811 if the [`capabilities` attribute](#capabilities-attribute) is also present,
1812 then `capabilities` MUST be processed before `modelsource`.
1813
1814 The serialization of this attribute MUST be semantically equivalent to
1815 what was used to create the model, but it is NOT REQUIRED to be syntactically
1816 equivalent. In other words, it might be "pretty-printed", but it MUST NOT
1817 include additional aspects even if those are defined/mandated by the
1818 specification or server implementation.
1819
1820- Constraints:
1821 - MUST NOT be included in API and document views unless requested, via the
1822 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
1823 - MUST be included in API and document views if requested, via the
1824 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
1825 - MAY be mutable based on the capabilities of the implementation.
1826
1827#### `<GROUPS>` Collections
1828- Type: Set of [Registry Collections](#registry-collections)
1829- Description: A list of Registry collections that contain the set of Groups
1830 supported by the Registry.
1831
1832- Constraints:
1833 - REQUIRED.
1834 - It MUST include all nested Group Collection types in the
1835 Registry, even if some of the collections are empty.
1836
1837### Registry Capabilities
1838
1839In order to programmatically discover which capabilities are supported by an
1840implementation, servers SHOULD support exposing this information via a
1841"capabilities" map that lists each supported feature along with any related
1842configuration detail that will help in successful usage of that feature.
1843
1844The "key" of the capabilities-map is the "name" of each feature, and the
1845"value" is a feature-specific set of configuration values, with the most basic
1846being a `<BOOLEAN>` value of `true` to indicate support for the feature.
1847
1848The JSON serialization of capabilities map MUST be of the form:
1849
1850```
1851{
1852 "available": { "<STRING>": { "mutable": <BOOLEAN> } + },
1853 "compatibilities": { "<STRING>": [ "<STRING>" * ] * }, ?
1854 "flags": [ "<STRING>" * ], ?
1855 "formats": [ "<STRING>" * ], ?
1856 "ignores": [ "<STRING>" * ], ?
1857 "mutable": [ "<STRING>" * ], ?
1858 "pagination": <BOOLEAN>, ?
1859 "shortself": <BOOLEAN>, ?
1860 "specversions": [ "<STRING>" ], ?
1861 "versionmodes": [ "<STRING>" ], ?
1862
1863 "<STRING>": ... capability configuration ... * // Extension capabilities
1864}
1865```
1866
1867Where:
1868- `"<STRING>"`, as a top-level key, MUST be the name of the capability. This
1869 specification places no restriction on the `"<STRING>"` value, other than it
1870 MUST be unique across all capabilities and not be an empty string. It is
1871 RECOMMENDED that extensions use some domain-specific name to avoid possible
1872 conflicts with other extensions.
1873
1874When serializing their supported capabilities, servers MUST include all
1875capabilities (including extensions) since the absence of a capability indicates
1876lack of support for that feature. However, absence, presence, or configuration
1877values of a feature in the map MAY vary based on the authorization level of
1878the client making the request.
1879
1880The list of values for the arrays MUST be case-insensitive and MAY include
1881extension values.
1882
1883For clarity, servers MUST include all supported capabilities in the
1884serialization, even if they are set to their default values or have empty
1885lists.
1886
1887It is RECOMMENDED that protocols for this specification support retrieval of
1888the capabilities via the inlining of the Registry entity's `capabilities`
1889attribute well as a stand-alone map independent of the Registry entity (e.g.
1890[`GET /capabilities`](./http.md#get-capabilities) in the HTTP case). However,
1891as with all interactions with a server, security/access controls MAY be
1892needed.
1893
1894The following defines the specification-defined capabilities:
1895
1896#### `available` Capability
1897- Name: `available`
1898- Type: Map of types of xRegistry metadata available.
1899- Description: The list of the various types of metadata available from this
1900 xRegistry instance. This information is meant to be used by clients, and
