1901 tooling, to programmatically discover which pieces of xRegistry information
1902 are available to query or edit.
1903
1904 The "key" of each map entry MUST be one of the defined values listed below.
1905 The "value" of each map entry MUST be an Object with a nested `"mutable"`
1906 boolean attribute indicating whether or not the corresponding data is
1907 user-editable.
1908
1909 Some of the items listed are available via more than one mechanism. For
1910 example, "model", in the HTTP protocol case, is available the `/model` API
1911 as well as via the `?inline=model` query parameter. In these cases, the data
1912 MUST be available via all supported retrieval mechanisms. For example, it
1913 would violate this specification if the `/model` API was supported but
1914 `?inline=model` was not, assuming the `?inline` flag was supported. If the
1915 `?inline` flag, in general, was not supported then only allowing the
1916 retrieval of the model via the `/model` API is permitted. Note that if
1917 a separate API is defined for a piece of data, it MUST be supported if that
1918 data type is listed in this capability.
1919
1920 Metadata not listed in this capability is to be assumed to be unavailable
1921 via all mechanisms. Attempts to access unavailable metadata MUST generate
1922 an error ([not_available](#not_available)).
1923
1924- Defined values (case-insensitive):
1925 - [`capabilities`](#registry-capabilities) (MUST always be present in the
1926 list)
1927 - [`capabilitiesoffered`](#offered-capabilities)
1928 - `entities` (xRegistry root entity, Groups, Resource and Versions. MUST
1929 always be present in the list.)
1930 - [`export`](#single-document-view) (Document view of entire registry.)
1931 - [`model`](#model-attribute) (MUST have a `mutable` value of `false`. MUST
1932 always be present in the list.)
1933 - [`modelsource`](#modelsource-attribute)
1934- When not specified, the default value MUST be:
1935 ```yaml
1936 {
1937 "capabilities": { "mutable": false },
1938 "entities": { "mutable": true },
1939 "model": { "mutable": false }
1940 }
1941 ```
1942- Implementations MAY define additional values.
1943- Implementations MAY define additional attributes for the nested Object.
1944- It is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that implementations also support at least
1945 `capabilities` and `model`.
1946- Examples:
1947 ```yaml
1948 "available": {
1949 "capabilities": { "mutable": false },
1950 "capabilitiesoffered": { "mutable": false },
1951 "entities": { "mutable": true },
1952 "export": { "mutable": false },
1953 "model": { "mutable": false },
1954 "modelsource": { "mutable": true }
1955 }
1956 ```
1957
1958#### `compatibilities` Capability
1959- Name: `compatibilities`
1960- Type: Map of compatibility rules per format
1961- Description: The set of compatibility rules that are available for each
1962 supported `format`. Each map key MUST be a case-insensitive [Capabilities
1963 `formats`](#formats-capability) value, and the map value MUST be the list of
1964 case-insensitive compatibility rules supported by that `format`. The key MAY
1965 include a `*` (wildcard) character that matches zero or more instances of any
1966 character at that location in the string. Similar to a `.*` in regular
1967 expressions.
1968
1969 An error
1970 ([capability_error](#capability_error)) MUST be generated if a specified
1971 key/format isn't in Capabilities `formats` list or the compatibility rule
1972 specified is not supported for that `format` (i.e. that combination of
1973 `format`/`compatibility` is not listed in the `compatibilities` offered
1974 capabilities).
1975
1976 Compatibility rules are semantic requirements that define how Versions of a
1977 Resource are allowed to change over time. For example, the compatibility rule
1978 of `backward` typically means that a newer Version of the Resource is
1979 backwards compatible with the next oldest Version of that Resource. What
1980 "backward compatible" means will vary based on what the Resource/Version
1981 represents. The Version's `format` attribute is meant to be the indicator
1982 as to "what" the Version is - which is why it is the "key" into this
1983 `compatibilities` map.
1984- When not specified, the default value MUST be an empty map and no support
1985 for Version compatibility is supported.
1986- Examples:
1987 - `"compatibilities": { "avro": [ "backward", "forward" ] }`
1988 - `"compatibilities": { "jsonschema*": [ "backward", "forward", "full" ] }`
1989
1990#### `flags` Capability
1991- Name: `flags`
1992- Type: Array of strings
1993- Description: The list of supported [Request Flags](#request-flags). Absence
1994 in the map indicates no support for that flag.
1995- Defined values (case-insensitive):
1996 `binary`, `collections`, `doc`, `epoch`, `filter`, `ignore`, `inline`,
1997 `setdefaultversionid`, `sort`, `specversion`.
1998- When not specified, the default value MUST be an empty list and no flags
1999 are supported.
2000- Examples:
2001 - `"flags": [ "filter", "inline" ]` # Just these 2
2002 - `"flags": [ "*" ]` # All supported flags (requests only)
2003
2004#### `formats` Capability
2005- Name: `formats`
2006- Type: Array of strings
2007- Description: The list of case-insensitive Version
2008 [`format`](#format-attribute) values that can be validated. An error
2009 ([capability_error](#capability_error)) MUST be generated if any value
2010 specified is not supported by the server (i.e. not listed in the `formats`
2011 offered capabilities).
2012- When not specified, the default value MUST be an empty list and no formats
2013 are supported.
2014- Examples:
2015 - `"formats": [ "avro/1.0", "protobuf/1.5", "jsonSchema*" ]`
2016
2017#### `ignores` Capability
2018- Name: `ignores`
2019- Type: Array of strings
2020- Description: The list of supported [Ignore Flag](#ignore-flag) values.
2021- Defined values (case-insensitive):
2022 `capabilities`, `defaultversionid`, `defaultversionsticky`, `id`, `epoch`,
2023 `modelsource`, `readonly`.
2024- When not specified, the default value MUST be an empty list and no ignore
2025 flags are supported.
2026- Examples:
2027 - `"ignores": [ "epoch", "id" ]` # Just these 2
2028 - `"ignores": [ "*" ]` # All supported values (requests only)
2029
2030#### `pagination` Capability
2031- Name: `pagination`
2032- Type: Boolean
2033- Description: Indicates whether the server supports the use of a
2034 protocol-specific "pagination" feature when querying xRegistry collections.
2035 Each protocol binding specification will define which pagination
2036 specification(s) is to be supported, if any.
2037- When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.
2038
2039#### `shortself` Capability
2040- Name: `shortself`
2041- Type: Boolean
2042- Description: Indicates whether the `shortself` attribute MUST be included
2043 in the server serialization of the entities within the Registry (value of
2044 `true`).
2045- When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.
2046
2047#### `specversions` Capability
2048- Name: `specversions`
2049- Type: Array of case-insensitive strings
2050- Description: List of xRegistry specification versions supported by the
2051 `specversion` flag.
2052- Non-exhaustive list of supported values:
2053 - `1.0-rc4`
2054- When not specified, the default value MUST be the latest version of this
2055 specification supported by the server.
2056
2057#### Updating the Capabilities of a Server
2058
2059Implementations MAY support clients updating the capabilities of the server.
2060If so, they SHOULD support it via updates to the Registry entity's
2061`capabilities` attribute as well as updates via a stand-alone map independent
2062of the Registry entity (e.g.
2063[`PUT /capabilities`](./http.md#patch-and-put-capabilities) in the HTTP case).
2064
2065The request to update the capabilities MUST include a serialization of the
2066capability map as described above. Whether it includes the full set of
2067supported capabilities or a subset will vary based on the protocol defined.
2068However, the following rules apply in both cases.
2069
2070For any capability that is an array of strings, a value of `"*"` MAY be used to
2071indicate that the server MUST replace `"*"` with the full set of items that
2072are available. An error ([capability_wildcard](#capability_wildcard)) MUST be
2073generated if `"*"` appears along with any other value in the list. `"*"`
2074MUST NOT appear in the serialization in any server's response.
2075
2076A request to update a capability with a value that is compliant with the
2077format of the `capabilities` definition MAY still generate an error
2078([capability_error](#capability_error)) if the server determines it cannot
2079support the request. For example, due to authorization concerns or the value,
2080while syntactically valid, isn't allowed in certain situations.
2081
2082A request to update a capability that doesn't include a mandatory value (such
2083as the current specification version for `specversions`), MUST generate an
2084error ([capability_missing_value](#capability_missing_value)).
2085
2086A request to update a capability with an invalid value MUST generate an error
2087([capability_value](#capability_value)).
2088
2089A request to update an unknown capability MUST generate an error
2090([capability_unknown](#capability_unknown)).
2091
2092Normally, modifying the capabilities of a server and modifying any entity data
2093are typically two very distinct actions, and will not typically happen at the
2094same time. However, if the situation does occur, a consistent (interoperable)
2095processing order needs to be defined. See the
2096[`capabilities` Attribute](#capabilities-attribute) section for more details.
2097
2098#### Offered Capabilities
2099
2100In order for an authorized client to update the capabilities of a server
2101it might need to first discover the list of available values for each
2102capability. This information is described via a map (similar to the capability
2103map itself) where each supported capability's name is the key of the
2104map, and the corresponding value provides details about the capability
2105(e.g. allowed values and pointer to its documentation).
2106
2107The JSON serialization of the capabilities offering map MUST be of the form:
2108
2109```yaml
2110{
2111 "<STRING>": { # Name of Capability attribute
2112 "type": "<TYPE>",
2113 "enum": [ <VALUE> * ], ? # Allowed values for scalars
2114 "min": <VALUE>, ?
2115 "max": <VALUE>, ?
2116 "documentation": "<URL>", ?
2117
2118 "attributes": { ... }, ? # If "type" is object
2119 "item": { # If "type" is map,array
2120 "type": "<TYPE>", # Value type of map, array type
2121 "attributes": { ... }, ? # If this item "type" is object (see above)
2122 "item": { ... } ? # If this item "type" is map,array (see above)
2123 }, ?
2124 } *
2125}
2126```
2127
2128Where:
2129- The top-level `"<STRING>"` MUST be the capability name.
2130- `<TYPE>` MUST be one of the data types specified in
2131 [Attributes and Extensions](#attributes-and-extensions).
2132- `"enum"`, when specified, contains a list of zero or more `<VALUE>`s whose
2133 type MUST match either `"type"` (when scalar) or `"item.type"` if `"type"`
2134 is `"array"` or `"map"` and `"item.type"` is a scalar.
2135- `"min"` and `"max"`, when specified, MUST match the same type as either
2136 `"type"` or `"item.type"` if `"type"` is `"array"` or `"map"`. These indicate
2137 the minimum or maximum (inclusive) value range of this capability. When not
2138 specified, there is no stated lower (or upper) limit. These MUST only be
2139 used when "type" is a numeric type.
2140- `"documentation"` provides a URL with additional information about the
2141 capability.
2142- `"attributes"`, when specified, contains the list (as a map) of attributes
2143 defined for the "object"-typed capability. This makes the schema of the
2144 capability recursive.
2145- `"item"` MUST be specified when `"type"` is `"array"` or `"map"`, and
2146 specify details about the items in the array, or values of the map.
2147 Note, all map keys MUST be of type string.
2148
2149Notice the syntax borrows much of the same structure from the
2150xRegistry [model definition](./model.md#registry-model) language.
2151
2152To maximize discoverability for clients, even in cases where there is no
2153variability allowed for certain capabilities, they MUST still be listed in
2154a server's "offering" serialization.
2155
2156For example, if `pagination` is not supported, but is a known feature, then a
2157server MUST still include:
2158
2159```yaml
2160 "pagination": {
2161 "type": "boolean",
2162 "enum": [ false ]
2163 }
2164```
2165
2166in the serialization of its capabilities offering map.
2167
2168**Examples:**
2169
2170```yaml
2171{
2172 "available": {
2173 "type": "object",
2174 "attributes": {
2175 "capabilities": {
2176 "type": "object",
2177 "attributes": { "mutable": { "type": "boolean" } }
2178 },
2179 "capabilitiesoffered": {
2180 "type": "object",
2181 "attributes": { "mutable": { "type": "boolean" } }
2182 },
2183 "entities": {
2184 "type": "object",
2185 "attributes": { "mutable": { "type": "boolean", "enum": [ false ] } }
2186 },
2187 "export": {
2188 "type": "object",
2189 "attributes": { "mutable": { "type": "boolean", "enum": [ false ] } }
2190 },
2191 "model": {
2192 "type": "object",
2193 "attributes": { "mutable": { "type": "boolean" } }
2194 },
2195 "modelsource": {
2196 "type": "object",
2197 "attributes": { "mutable": { "type": "boolean" } }
2198 }
2199 }
2200 },
2201 "compatibilities": {
2202 "type": "object",
2203 "attributes": {
2204 "avro": {
2205 "type": "array",
2206 "item": { "type": "string" },
2207 "enum": [ "backward", "forward" ]
2208 },
2209 "protobuf": {
2210 "type": "array",
2211 "item": { "type": "string" },
2212 "enum": [ "backward" ]
2213 }
2214 }
2215 },
2216 "flags": {
2217 "type": "array",
2218 "item": {
2219 "type": "string"
2220 },
2221 "enum": [ "binary", "collections", "doc", "epoch", "filter", "ignore",
2222 "inline", "setdefaultversionid", "sort", "specversion" ]
2223 },
2224 "formats": {
2225 "type": "array",
2226 "item": {
2227 "type": "string"
2228 },
2229 "enum": [ "avro", "protobuf", "jsonSchema" ]
2230 },
2231 "ignores": {
2232 "type": "array",
2233 "item": {
2234 "type": "string"
2235 },
2236 "enum": [ "capabilities", "defaultversionid", "defaultversionsticky",
2237 "epoch", "id", "modelsource", "readonly" ]
2238 },
2239 "mutable": {
2240 "type": "array",
2241 "enum": [ "capabilities", "entities", "modelsource" ],
2242 "item": {
2243 "type": "string"
2244 }
2245 },
2246 "pagination": {
2247 "type": "boolean",
2248 "enum": [ false, true ]
2249 },
2250 "shortself": {
2251 "type": "boolean",
2252 "enum": [ false, true ]
2253 },
2254 "specversions": {
2255 "type": "array",
2256 "enum": [ "1.0-rc4" ],
2257 "item": {
2258 "type": "string"
2259 }
2260 },
2261 "versionmodes": {
2262 "type": "array",
2263 "enum": [ "manual", "createdat", "modifiedat", "semver" ],
2264 "item": {
2265 "type": "string"
2266 }
2267 }
2268}
2269```
2270
2271### Group Entity
2272
2273Groups represent entities that typically act as a collection mechanism for
2274related Resources. However, it is worth noting that Groups do not have to have
2275Resources associated with them. It is possible to have Groups be the main (or
2276only) entity of a Registry. Each Group type MAY have any number of Resource
2277types within it. This specification does not define how the Resources within a
2278Group type are related to each other.
2279
2280The serialization of a Group entity MUST adhere to this form:
2281
2282```yaml
2283{
2284 "<GROUP>id": "<STRING>",
2285 "self": "<URL>",
2286 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
2287 "xid": "<XID>",
2288 "epoch": <UINTEGER>,
2289 "name": "<STRING>", ?
2290 "description": "<STRING>", ?
2291 "documentation": "<URL>", ?
2292 "icon": "<URL>", ?
2293 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ?
2294 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
2295 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
2296 "deprecated": {
2297 "effective": "<TIMESTAMP>", ?
2298 "removal": "<TIMESTAMP>", ?
2299 "alternative": "<URL>", ?
2300 "documentation": "<URL>"?
2301 }, ?
2302
2303 # Repeat for each Resource type in the Group
2304 "<RESOURCES>url": "<URL>", # e.g. "messagesurl"
2305 "<RESOURCES>count": <UINTEGER>, # e.g. "messagescount"
2306 "<RESOURCES>": { Resources collection } ? # If inlined
2307}
2308```
2309
2310Group extension attributes would also appear as additional top-level JSON
2311attributes.
2312
2313Groups include the following
2314[common attributes](#common-attributes):
2315- [`<GROUP>id`](#singularid-id-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2316 OPTIONAL in requests.
2317- [`self`](#self-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2318 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
2319- [`shortself`](#shortself-attribute) - OPTIONAL in API and document views,
2320 based on the `shortself` capability. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
2321- [`xid`](#xid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2322 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
2323- [`epoch`](#epoch-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL in
2324 requests.
2325- [`name`](#name-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
2326- [`description`](#description-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
2327- [`documentation`](#documentation-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
2328- [`icon`](#icon-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
2329- [`labels`](#labels-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
2330- [`createdat`](#createdat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2331 OPTIONAL in requests.
2332- [`modifiedat`](#modifiedat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2333 OPTIONAL in requests.
2334- [`deprecated`](#deprecated-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
2335
2336and the following Group-level attributes:
2337
2338#### `<RESOURCES>` Collections
2339- Type: Set of [Registry Collections](#registry-collections).
2340- Description: A list of Registry collections that contain the set of
2341 Resources supported by the Group.
2342
2343- Constraints:
2344 - REQUIRED.
2345 - It MUST include all nested Resource Collection types of the owning Group,
2346 even if some of the collections are empty.
2347
2348### Resource Entity
2349
2350Resources typically represent the main entity that the Registry is managing.
2351Each Resource is associated with a Group to aid in their discovery and to show
2352a relationship with Resources in that same Group. Resources appear within the
2353Group's `<RESOURCES>` collection.
2354
2355Resources, like all entities in the Registry, can be modified but Resources
2356can also have a version history associated with them, allowing for users to
2357retrieve previous Versions of the Resource. In this respect, Resources have
2358a 2-layered definition. The first layer is the Resource entity itself,
2359and the second layer is its `versions` collection - the version history of
2360the Resource.
2361
2362The Resource entity serves three purposes:
2363
23641. It represents the collection of historical Versions of the data being
2365 managed. This is true even if the Resource type is defined to not use
2366 versioning, meaning the number of Versions allowed is just one. The
2367 Versions will appear as a nested xRegistry collection under the `versions`
2368 attribute.
2369
23702. It acts as an alias for the "default" Version of the Resource. This means
2371 that any operation (read or write) that deals with attributes exposed via
2372 the Resource, but are inherited from the "default" Version, MUST
2373 act upon that Version's corresponding attribute. See
2374 [Default Version of a Resource](#default-version-of-a-resource),
2375 [Updating Nested Registry
2376 Collections](#updating-nested-registry-collections)
2377 and [Version Entity](#version-entity) for additional semantics that apply
2378 to write operations on Resources.
2379
23803. It has a set of attributes for Resource-level metadata - data that is not
2381 specific to one Version of the Resource but instead applies to the
2382 Resource in general. Most of these attributes appear under a
2383 [`meta` entity](#meta-entity) so as to keep them separate
2384 from any default Version-level attributes that might appear. Note that
2385 these attributes do not appear on the Versions.
2386
2387When a Resource is serialized as xRegistry metadata without the inherited
2388default Version attributes, such as when the [`doc` flag](#doc-flag) is used,
2389it MUST adhere to the following:
2390
2391```yaml
2392{
2393 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>",
2394 "self": "<URL>", # URL to Resource, not Version
2395 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
2396 "xid": "<XID>", # Relative URI to Resource
2397
2398 "metaurl": "<URL>", # URL to 'meta' entity
2399 "meta": { meta entity }, ? # Only if inlined
2400 "versionsurl": "<URL>", # Absolute URL to versions
2401 "versionscount": <UINTEGER>, # Size of versions collection
2402 "versions": { map of Versions } # Only if inlined
2403}
2404```
2405
2406When the default Version attributes do appear in the xRegistry metadata
2407serialization of the Resource (e.g. the [`doc` flag](#doc-flag) is not used)
2408it MUST adhere to the following:
2409
2410```yaml
2411{
2412 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>",
2413 "versionid": "<STRING>", # Default Version's ID
2414 "self": "<URL>",
2415 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
2416 "xid": "<XID>",
2417 "epoch": <UINTEGER>, # Start of default Ver attributes
2418 "name": "<STRING>", ?
2419 "isdefault": true,
2420 "description": "<STRING>", ?
2421 "documentation": "<URL>", ?
2422 "icon": "<URL>", ?
2423 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ?
2424 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
2425 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
2426 "ancestorid": "<STRING>",
2427 "contenttype": "<STRING>", ?
2428
2429 "<RESOURCE>url": "<URL>", ? # If not local
2430 "<RESOURCE>": ... Resource document ..., ? # If local & inlined & JSON
2431 "<RESOURCE>base64": "<STRING>", ? # If local & inlined & ~JSON
2432 # End of default Ver attributes
2433 "metaurl": "<URL>",
2434 "meta": { meta entity }, ? # Only if inlined
2435 "versionsurl": "<URL>",
2436 "versionscount": <UINTEGER>,
2437 "versions": { map of Versions } ? # Only if inlined
2438}
2439```
2440
2441Note that the Version attributes that conflict with the Resource
2442attributes (e.g. `self`, `shortself`, `xid`) are not inherited by this
2443serialization. Their values are for the Resource and not the default
2444Version's.
2445
2446#### Resource Attributes
2447
2448The Resource entity includes the following
2449[common attributes](#common-attributes):
2450- [`<RESOURCE>id`](#singularid-id-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document
2451 views. OPTIONAL in requests.
2452- [`self`](#self-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2453 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. References the Resource, not the default
2454 Version.
2455- [`shortself`](#shortself-attribute) - OPTIONAL in API and document views,
2456 based on the `shortself` capability. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
2457 References the Resource, not the default Version.
2458- [`xid`](#xid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2459 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. References the Resource, not the default
2460 Version.
2461
2462and the following Resource-level attributes:
2463
2464##### `metaurl` Attribute
2465- Type: URL
2466- Description: A server-generated URL referencing the Resource's
2467 [`meta` entity](#meta-entity).
2468
2469- API View Constraints:
2470 - REQUIRED.
2471 - MUST be immutable.
2472 - MUST be an absolute URL to the Resource's `meta` entity.
2473 - MUST be a read-only attribute.
2474
2475- Document View Constraints:
2476 - REQUIRED.
2477 - If the `meta` entity is inlined in the document, then this attribute
2478 MUST be a relative URL of the form `#JSON-POINTER` where the `JSON-POINTER`
2479 locates the `meta` entity within the current document. See
2480 [Doc Flag](#doc-flag) for more information.
2481 - If the `meta` entity is not inlined in the document, then this attribute
2482 MUST be an absolute URL per the API view constraints listed above.
2483
2484- Examples:
2485 - `https://example.com/endpoints/ep1/messages/msg1/meta` (API view)
2486 - `#/endpoints/ep1/messages/msg1/meta` (Document view)
2487
2488##### `meta` Attribute
2489- Type: Object
2490- Description: An object that contains most of the Resource-level attributes.
2491
2492 See [Meta Entity](#meta-entity) for more information.
2493
2494 During a write operation, the absence of the `meta` attribute in the request
2495 indicates that no changes are to be made to the `meta` entity.
2496
2497- Constraints:
2498 - MUST NOT be included in API and document views unless requested via the
2499 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
2500 - MUST be included in API and document views if requested via the
2501 [Inline Flag](#inline-flag).
2502
2503##### `versions` Collection
2504- Type: [Registry Collection](#registry-collections)
2505- Description: The set of xRegistry Version entities for the Resource.
2506
2507 Note that Resources MUST have at least one Version.
2508
2509- Constraints:
2510 - REQUIRED.
2511
2512#### Resource Metadata vs Resource Document
2513
2514Unlike Groups, which consist entirely of xRegistry managed metadata, Resource
2515Versions often have their own domain-specific data and document format that
2516needs to be kept distinct from the xRegistry Version metadata. As discussed
2517previously, the model definition for Resource types has a
2518[`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
2519indicating whether a Resource type defines its own separate document or not.
2520
2521This specification does not define any requirements for the contents of this
2522separate document, and it doesn't even need to be stored within the Registry.
2523The Version MAY choose to simply store a URL reference to the externally
2524managed document instead. When the document is stored within the Registry, it
2525can be managed as an opaque array of bytes and is available via the Version
2526[`<RESOURCE>`](#resource-attribute) or
2527[`<RESOURCE>base64`](#resourcebase64-attribute) attributes.
2528
2529When a Resource is configured to possibly have a separate document, clients
2530can choose whether they want to interact with that document or with the
2531xRegistry metadata. In this sense, there are two "views" of the
2532Resource/Version that client can choose from.
2533
2534Each xRegistry binding specification will define the mechanism by which clients
2535can indicate which view of the Resource/Version they want to interact with.
2536For HTTP, see the
2537[Resource Metadata vs Resource Document](./http.md#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document)
2538section for more information, in particular about the use of the `$details`
2539URL suffix. Those specifications will also define any protocol-specific
2540serialization rules when the Resource domain-specific document view is used.
2541
2542#### Creating or Updating Resources and Versions
2543
2544The following rules apply to the processing of write operations for
2545Resources and Versions:
2546
2547- If a Resource exists with only one Version then it MUST become the "default"
2548 Version.
2549- If more than one Version is created at the same time as the owning Resource
2550 is created, and the `meta.defaultversionid` is not set as part of the
2551 request, then use of the
2552 [SetDefaultVersionID Flag](#setdefaultversionid-flag) is RECOMMENDED. See
2553 [Default Version of a Resource](#default-version-of-a-resource) for more
2554 information.
2555
2556The following sections go into more details about the processing of requests
2557to create/update Resources and Versions.
2558
2559##### Resource Processing Algorithm
2560
2561Processing of a request to create/update a Resource has many different aspects
2562to consider. The following describes the general algorithm that servers are
2563expected to follow. Implementations are not mandated to follow this exact
2564sequence of actions but the net semantic results MUST be adhered to.
2565
2566Users of Registries will most likely not need to understand all of the details
2567mentioned in this section. Additionally, users are encouraged to limit
2568themselves to operations that modify one entity at a time whenever possible to
2569keep the interactions simple (e.g. operate on single Versions directly rather
2570than the entire `versions` collection in one request). Then operations that
2571need the level of complexity detailed in this section would only be needed for
2572"import" type of cases.
2573
2574For this discussion, it is assumed that some variant of the Resource's JSON
2575is present in a write operation request, as shown in the following abbreviated
2576JSON serialization:
2577
2578```yaml
2579{
2580 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>",
2581 "versionid": "<STRING>",
2582 "epoch": <UINTEGER>,
2583 "isdefault": true,
2584 ... other default Version attributes ...
2585
2586 "meta": {
2587 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>",
2588 "xref": "<XID>",
2589 "epoch": <UINTEGER>,
2590 "defaultversionid": "<STRING>",
2591 "defaultversionsticky": <BOOLEAN>
2592 ... other meta-level attributes ...
2593 },
2594
2595 "versions": { ... map of Versions ... }
2596}
2597```
2598
2599Notice that the serialization can be broken into 3 distinct parts:
2600- The Resource's default Version attributes.
2601- The `meta` sub-object.
2602- The `versions` collection of Resource Versions.
2603
2604The overall processing of the request message is as follows:
2605
26061. Process the Versions in the `versions` collection, if present.
26072. Process the Resource's default Version attributes only if the default
2608 Version is not present in the `versions` collection.
26093. Update all Version's [`ancestorid` values](#ancestorid-attribute) as needed,
2610 based on the Resource's
2611 [`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) value.
26124. Process the `meta` sub-object, if present.
26135. Update [`meta.defaultversionid`](#defaultversionid-attribute) as needed.
26146. Enforce the [Version format checks](#format-attribute).
26157. Enforce the [Group-level constraints](./model.md#groupsstringconstraints).
26168. Enforce the [Resource `matchversions`
2617 checks](./model.md#attributesstringmatchversions).
26189. Enforce the [Version compatibility checks](#compatibility-attribute).
261910. Enforce the [Resource `maxversions`
2620 constraints](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringmaxversions). Note that
2621 this might require updating the [`ancestorid` values](#ancestorid-attribute)
2622 again after some Versions have been deleted.
2623
2624The following provides additional details:
2625
2626- Implementation optimizations:
2627 - Implementations MAY choose to optimize the order in which the incoming
2628 request's data is processed as long as the net semantic results are as
2629 defined by this specification.
2630 - For example:
2631 - "fail-fast" error checking is RECOMMENDED.
2632 - Determining if the resulting Resource has a non-empty `meta.xref` value
2633 might allow for skipping unnecessary work.
2634
2635- Step 2 - Processing the Resource's default Version attributes:
2636 - In this step the Resource's default Version (as defined prior to the
2637 start of the operation) is to be updated with the Resource-level attributes
2638 specified in the request. Note that an empty list of attributes, when not
2639 doing a patch type of operation, will reset all attributes to their default
2640 values.
2641 - However, when the Resource is created as part of the current operation
2642 there is no "prior" default Version, so knowing how to apply those
2643 attributes requires some additional clarity:
2644 - If a Resource-level `versionid` attribute is present, and that Version
2645 is not in the request's `versions` collection, then a new Version with
2646 that `versionid` MUST be created with the Resource-level attributes. If
2647 it is in the `versions` collection then the Resource-level attributes
2648 MUST be ignored.
2649 - If `versionid` is not present, but `meta.defaultversionid` is present,
2650 and that Version is not in the request's `versions` collection, then a
2651 new Version with that `versionid` MUST be created, with the
2652 Resource-level attributes. If it is in the `versions` collection then
2653 the Resource-level attributes MUST be ignored. Also see
2654 [SetDefaultVersionID Flag](#setdefaultversionid-flag) for an additional
2655 mechanism by which it might be set.
2656 - If neither of those attributes are present, then the `versions`
2657 collection will dictate the result:
2658 - If `versions` is missing, or empty, then the server MUST generate a
2659 new unique [`versionid` value](#version-ids) and create a new Version
2660 using that value, with the Resource-level attributes.
2661 - If `versions` is present with at least one Version, then the
2662 Resource-level attributes MUST be ignored. This is because without
2663 any indication from the client as to which Version the Resource-level
2664 attributes need to be applied to, rather than creating a new Version,
2665 the assumption is that `versions` contains all of the Versions that are
2666 meant to be created.
2667 - If the operation is converting a cross-reference Resource back into a
2668 "normal" Resource then the new Version created MUST adhere the rules
2669 specified in the
2670 [Cross Referencing Resources](#cross-referencing-resources) section.
2671
2672See [Resource Update Samples](./resource.md) for examples.
2673
2674##### `<RESOURCE>*` Attribute Processing
2675
2676The processing of the 3 `<RESOURCE>*` attributes MUST follow these rules:
2677
2678 - At most, only one of the 3 attributes MAY be present in the request, and
2679 the presence of any one of them MUST delete the other 2 attributes.
2680 Otherwise an error ([one_resource](#one_resource)) MUST be generated.
2681 - If the entity already exists and its `<RESOURCE>url` has no value,
2682 then absence of all 3 attributes MUST leave all 3 unchanged.
2683 - An explicit value of `null` for any of the 3 attributes MUST result in
2684 same net effect as defining the entity's domain-specific document to be
2685 an empty document.
2686 - When `<RESOURCE>` is present, the server MAY choose to modify non-semantic
2687 significant characters. For example, to remove (or add) whitespace. In
2688 other words, there is no requirement for the server to persist the
2689 document in the exact byte-for-byte format in which it was provided. If
2690 that is desired then clients MUST use `<RESOURCE>base64` instead.
2691 - On a non-patch type of write operation, when `<RESOURCE>` is present,
2692 if no `contenttype` value is provided then the server MUST set it to the
2693 same type as the incoming request, e.g. `application/json`, even if the
2694 entity previously had a `contenttype` value.
2695 - On a patch type of operation, when `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` is
2696 present, if no `contenttype` value is provided then the server MUST set it
2697 to the same type as the incoming request, e.g. `application/json`, only if
2698 the entity does not already have a value. Otherwise, the existing value
2699 remains unchanged.
2700
2701#### Cross Referencing Resources
2702
2703Typically, Resources exist within the scope of a single Group, however there
2704might be situations where a Resource needs to be related to multiple Groups.
2705In these cases, there are two options. First, a copy of the Resource could be
2706made into the second Group. The obvious downside to this is that there's no
2707relationship between the two Resources and any changes to one would need to
2708be done in the other - running the risk of them getting out of sync.
2709
2710The second, and better, option is to create a cross-reference from one
2711(the "source" Resource) to the other ("target" Resource). This is done
2712by setting the `meta.xref` attribute on the source Resource to be the `xid`
2713of the target Resource, thus making the "source" Resource look like the
2714"target" Resource.
2715
2716For example: a `schema` Resource instance defined as:
2717
2718```yaml
2719{
2720 "schemaid": "mySchema",
2721 "meta": {
2722 "xref": "/schemagroups/group2/schemas/sharedSchema"
2723 }
2724}
2725```
2726
2727means that `mySchema` references `sharedSchema`, which exists in `group2`.
2728When this source Resource (`mySchema`) is retrieved, all of the target
2729Resource's attributes (except its `<RESOURCE>id`) will appear as if they were
2730locally defined.
2731
2732So, if the target Resource (`sharedSchema`) is defined as:
2733
2734```yaml
2735{
2736 "resourceid": "sharedSchema",
2737 "versionid": "v1",
2738 "self": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group2/schemas/sharedSchema",
2739 "xid": "/schemagroups/group2/schemas/sharedSchema",
2740 "epoch": 2,
2741 "isdefault": true,
2742 "createdat": "2024-01-01-T12:00:00Z",
2743 "modifiedat": "2024-01-01-T12:01:00Z",
2744 "ancestorid": "v1",
2745
2746 "metaurl": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group2/schemas/sharedSchema/meta",
2747 "versionscount": 1,
2748 "versionsurl": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group2/schemas/sharedSchema/versions"
2749}
2750```
2751
2752then the resulting serialization of the source Resource would be:
2753
2754```yaml
2755{
2756 "resourceid": "mySchema",
2757 "versionid": "v1",
2758 "self": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema",
2759 "xid": "/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema",
2760 "epoch": 2,
2761 "isdefault": true,
2762 "createdat": "2024-01-01-T12:00:00Z",
2763 "modifiedat": "2024-01-01-T12:01:00Z",
2764 "ancestorid": "v1",
2765
2766 "metaurl": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/meta",
2767 "meta": {
2768 "resourceid": "mySchema",
2769 "self": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/meta",
2770 "xid": "/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/meta",
2771 "xref": "/schemagroups/group2/schemas/sharedSchema",
2772 "createdat": "2024-01-01-T12:00:00Z",
2773 "modifiedat": "2024-01-01-T12:01:00Z",
2774 "readonly": false,
2775 "defaultversionid": "v1",
2776 "defaultversionurl": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/versions/v1",
2777 "defaultversionsticky": false
2778 },
2779 "versionscount": 1,
2780 "versionsurl": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/versions"
2781}
2782```
2783
2784Note:
2785- Any attributes referencing the source MUST use the source's metadata. In
2786 this respect, users of this serialization would never know that this is a
2787 cross-referenced Resource except for the presence of the `meta.xref`
2788 attribute. For example, its `<RESOURCE>id` MUST be the source's `id` and not
2789 the target's.
2790- The `xref` attribute MUST always appear when the source's `meta` sub-object
2791 is serialized so clients can easily determine that this Resource is a
2792 cross-referenced Resource.
2793- The `xref` XID MUST be the `xid` of the target Resource.
2794
2795From a consumption (read) perspective, aside from the presence of the `xref`
2796attribute, the Resource appears to be a normal Resource that exists within
2797`group1`. All of the specification-defined features (e.g. `inline`,
2798`filter` request flags) MAY be used when retrieving the Resource.
2799
2800However, from a write perspective it is quite different. In order to update
2801the target Resource's attributes (or nested entities), a write operation MUST
2802be done on the appropriate target Resource entity directly. Write
2803operations on the source MAY be done, however, the changes are limited to
2804converting it from a "cross-reference" Resource back into a "normal"
2805Resource. See the following for more information:
2806
2807When converting a "normal" Resource into a cross-reference Resource (adding
2808an `xref` value), or creating/updating a Resource that is a cross-reference
2809Resource, the following MUST be adhered to:
2810- The request MUST include an `xref` attribute with a value that is
2811 the `xid` of the target Resource.
2812- The request MAY include the `<RESOURCE>id` attribute (of the source
2813 Resource) on the Resource or `meta` entity.
2814- The request MAY include `epoch` within `meta` (to do an `epoch` validation
2815 check) only if the Resource already exists as a normal Resource.
2816- The request MUST NOT include nested collections or any other attributes
2817 (for the Resource or its "meta" entity). This includes default Version
2818 attributes within the Resource serialization. Presence of these extra
2819 attributes MUST generate an error
2820 ([extra_xref_attribute](#extra_xref_attribute)).
2821- If the Resource already exists, as a "normal" Resource, then any Versions
2822 associated with the Resource MUST be deleted.
2823
2824When converting a cross-reference Resource back into a "normal" Resource, the
2825following MUST be adhered to:
2826- The request MUST delete the `xref` attribute or set it to `null`.
2827- A default Version of the Resource MUST be created.
2828- Any attributes specified at the Resource level MUST be interpreted as a
2829 request to set the default Version attributes. Absence of any attributes
2830 MUST result in a default Version being created with all attributes set
2831 to their default values. Note that normal Resource update semantics apply.
2832 See [Creating or Updating Resources and
2833 Versions](#creating-or-updating-resources-and-versions) for more
2834 information.
2835- When not specified in the request, the Resource's `meta.createdat` value
2836 MUST be reset to the timestamp of when this source Resource was originally
2837 created.
2838- When not specified in the request, the Resource's `meta.modifiedat` value
2839 MUST be set to "now".
2840- The Resource's `meta.epoch` value MUST be greater than the original
2841 Resource's previously known value (if any) and greater than the target
2842 Resource's `meta.epoch` value. In pseudocode this is:
2843 `epoch = max(original_Epoch, target_Resource_Epoch) + 1`.
2844 This will ensure that the Resource's `epoch` value will never decrease as a
2845 result of this operation. Note that going from a "normal" Resource to a
2846 cross-reference Resource does not have this guarantee. If the target Resource
2847 no longer exists then `target_Resource_Epoch` MUST be treated as zero.
2848- Aside from the processing rules specified above, the Resource's attributes
2849 that might have existed prior to the Resource being converted from a
2850 "normal" Resource into a cross-reference Resource MUST NOT be resurrected
2851 with their old values.
2852- Any relationship with the target Resource MUST be deleted.
2853
2854If the target Resource itself is a cross-reference Resource, then including
2855the target Resource's attributes MUST NOT be done when serializing the
2856source Resource. Recursive, or transitively, following of `xref` XIDs is not
2857done.
2858
2859Both the source and target Resources MUST be of the same Resource model type,
2860simply having similar Resource type definitions is not sufficient. This
2861implies that the
2862[`ximportresources`](./model.md#groupsstringximportresources) feature to
2863reference a Resource type from another Group type definition MUST be
2864used.
2865
2866An `xref` value that points to a non-existing Resource, either because
2867it was deleted, never existed or the current client does not have permission
2868to see it, is not an error and is not a condition that a server is REQUIRED to
2869detect. In these "dangling xref" situations, the serialization of the source
2870Resource will not include any target Resource attributes or nested collections.
2871Rather, it will only show the `xref` and ID-like attributes. Therefore, a
2872client that receives a response containing only those attributes can
2873treat this as an indicator that the target Resource is inaccessible, and can
2874make the determination as to whether this is something to investigate or not.
2875
2876For example, a schema Resource (`mySchema`) referencing a non-existing schema
2877Resource (`missingSchema`) would look like:
2878
2879```yaml
2880{
2881 "schemaid": "mySchema",
2882 "self": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema",
2883 "xid": "/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema",
2884 "metaurl": "https://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/meta",
2885 "meta": {
2886 "schemaid": "mySchema",
2887 "self": "http://example.com/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/meta",
2888 "xid": "/schemagroups/group1/schemas/mySchema/meta",
2889 "xref": "/schemagroups/group1/schemas/missingSchema"
2890 }
2891}
2892```
2893
2894However, a non-existing Resource is not the same as a poorly formed XID
2895value. An `xref` that isn't syntactically correct, or references a
2896non-existing Group type or Resource type , MUST generate an error
2897([malformed_xref](#malformed_xref)).
2898
2899### Meta Entity
2900
2901The `meta` entity (within a Resource) contains most of the Resource-level
2902attributes that are global to the Resource, and not Version specific. It is
2903an entity in its own right, meaning it supports the normal "read" and "write"
2904operation targeted directly to it.
2905
2906Each Resource MUST have a Meta entity, and when the Resource is deleted then
2907the Meta entity MUST also be deleted. Delete requests directed to the Meta
2908entity MUST generate an error
2909([action_not_supported](./spec.md#action_not_supported)).
2910
2911A non-patch type of write operation that includes a Resource, as a mechanism
2912to update its `meta` entity would need to include the Resource's default
2913Version attributes in the request. If not, the server will interpret it as a
2914request to delete the default Version attributes, which is probably not the
2915desired result. Instead, a write operation directly targeted to the `meta`
2916entity would be a better choice, or a "patch" type of operation where only
2917the `meta` entity is included in the request.
2918
2919The serialization of the Meta entity MUST adhere to this form:
2920
2921```yaml
2922{
2923 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>", # Resource ID
2924 "self": "<URL>", # URL to this "meta" entity
2925 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
2926 "xid": "<XID>", # Relative URI to this "meta"
2927 "xref": "<XID>", ? # Ptr to linked Resource
2928 "epoch": <UINTEGER>, # Resource's epoch
2929 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ?
2930 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>", # Resource's
2931 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>", # Resource's
2932 "readonly": <BOOLEAN>, # Default=false
2933 "compatibility": "<STRING>", ?
2934 "deprecated": { ... }, ?
2935
2936 "defaultversionid": "<STRING>",
2937 "defaultversionurl": "<URL>",
2938 "defaultversionsticky": <BOOLEAN> ?
2939}
2940```
2941
2942Meta extension attributes would also appear as additional top-level JSON
2943attributes.
2944
2945The Meta entity includes the following
2946[common attributes](#common-attributes):
2947- [`<RESOURCE>id`](#singularid-id-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document
2948 views. OPTIONAL in requests.
2949- [`self`](#self-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2950 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. References the Meta entity, not the Resource.
2951- [`shortself`](#shortself-attribute) - OPTIONAL in API and document views,
2952 based on the `shortself` capability. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
2953 References the Meta entity, not the Resource.
2954- [`xid`](#xid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2955 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. References the Meta entity, not the Resource.
2956- [`epoch`](#epoch-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL
2957 in requests. This represents the `epoch` value of the entire Resource,
2958 not of one particular Version. And, it adheres to the normal `epoch`
2959 processing rules - its value is only updated when the Meta attributes
2960 are updated, and also when a Version is added/removed.
2961- [`labels`](#labels-attribute) - OPTIONAL in API and document views.
2962- [`createdat`](#createdat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2963 OPTIONAL in requests. Creation date of the Resource/Meta entity.
2964- [`modifiedat`](#modifiedat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
2965 OPTIONAL in requests. Modification date of the Meta entity. This will change
2966 at the same time that `epoch` changes.
2967- [`deprecated`](#deprecated-attribute) - OPTIONAL. Deprecated state of the
2968 entire Resource.
2969
2970and the following Meta-level attributes:
2971
2972#### `xref` Attribute
2973- Type: XID
2974- Description: Indicates that this Resource is a reference to another Resource
2975 within the same Registry. See [Cross Referencing
2976 Resources](#cross-referencing-resources) for more information.
2977
2978- Constraints:
2979 - OPTIONAL.
2980 - If present, it MUST be the case-sensitive `xid` of a same-typed Resource
2981 in the Registry.
2982
2983#### `readonly` Attribute
2984- Type: Boolean
2985- Description: Indicates whether this Resource is updateable by clients. This
2986 attribute is a server-controlled attribute and therefore MUST NOT be
2987 modifiable by non-admin clients. This specification makes no statement as to
2988 when Resources are to be read-only.
2989
2990 It is expected that only certain clients (e.g. "admin" clients) would be
2991 allowed to edit this attribute. This specification makes no statement as to
2992 how admin clients are defined or recognized by the server.
2993
2994- Constraints:
2995 - REQUIRED.
2996 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute for non-admin users.
2997 - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.
2998 - It MUST be a case-sensitive `true` or `false`.
2999 - A request to update a read-only Resource SHOULD generate an error
3000 ([readonly](#readonly)) unless the
3001 [Ignore Flag](#ignore-flag) was used with the `readonly` value, in which
3002 case the error MUST be silently ignored, and the Resource MUST remain
3003 unchanged.
3004
3005#### `compatibility` Attribute
3006- Type: String (with Resource-specified enumeration of possible values)
3007- Description: States that Versions of this Resource adhere to a certain
3008 compatibility rule. For example, a `backward` compatibility value would
3009 indicate that all Versions of a Resource are backwards compatible with the
3010 next oldest Version, as determined by their `ancestorid` attributes.
3011
3012 This specification makes no statement as to which parts of the Version data
3013 are examined for compatibility (e.g. xRegistry metadata, domain-specific
3014 document, etc.). This will be defined by the compatibility rules defined by
3015 each Version's `format` value.
3016
3017 The exact meaning of what each `compatibility` value means might vary based
3018 on the `format` value, therefore this specification only defines a very
3019 high-level abstract meaning for each to ensure some degree of consistency.
3020 However, domain-specific specifications are expected to modify the
3021 `compatibility` enum values defined in the Resource's model to limit the
3022 list of available values and to define the exact meaning of each.
3023
3024 For `compatibility` strategies that require understanding the lineage
3025 relationship between the Versions, the [`ancestorid`](#ancestorid-attribute)
3026 attribute on each Version MUST be used to determine that information.
3027
3028 This specification defines the following enumeration values. Implementations
3029 MAY choose to extend this list, or use a subset of it.
3030 - `backward` - A Version is compatible with the next oldest Version.
3031 - `backward_transitive` - A Version is compatible with all older Versions.
3032 - `forward` - A Version is compatible with the next newest Version.
3033 - `forward_transitive` - A Version is compatible with all newer Versions.
3034 - `full` - A Version is compatible with the next oldest and next newest
3035 Versions.
3036 - `full_transitive` - A Version is compatible with all older and all newer
3037 Versions.
3038
3039 When not specified, there is no statement being made as to the compatibility
3040 relationship between the Resource's Versions and the server MUST NOT perform
3041 any `compatibility` checking.
3042
3043- Constraints:
3044 - OPTIONAL.
3045 - If present, MUST be a case-insensitive non-empty value from the Registry's
3046 [`capabilities.compatibilities`](#compatibilities-capability) values
3047 for the set of `format` values used by the Versions of the Resource.
3048 - When changing the value of this attribute, it MUST be applied to all
3049 Versions of the Resource, and an error
3050 ([compatibility_violation](#compatibility_violation)) MUST be generated
3051 if any Version can not conform to the requirements of the specified
3052 compatibility value.
3053
3054#### `defaultversionid` Attribute
3055- Type: String
3056- Description: The case-sensitive `versionid` of the default Version of the
3057 Resource.
3058
3059- Constraints:
3060 - REQUIRED.
3061 - MUST be the `versionid` of the default Version of the Resource.
3062
3063When a "patch" type of operation is used and this attribute is present in the
3064request but `defaultversionsticky` is absent, then:
3065 - A non-`null` value MUST set `defaultversionsticky` to `true`.
3066 - A `null` value MUST set `defaultversionsticky` to `false`.
3067
3068At the end of an update operation, this attribute MUST be set according to the
3069[`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) value
3070of the Resource in any of the following situations:
3071- The resulting `defaultversionsticky` value is `false`.
3072- The processing fully replaced the `meta` sub-object and the request included
3073 `defaultversionsticky` with a value of `true`, but no `defaultversionid` was
3074 provided.
3075- The processing patched the `meta` sub-object and the request modified
3076 `defaultversionsticky` from `false` to `true`, but no `defaultversionid`
3077 was provided.
3078
3079Regardless of the reason for `defaultversionid` or `defaultversionsticky`
3080being modified, those changes alone MUST NOT change any attributes in any
3081Version of the Resource. For example, attributes such as `modifiedat` and
3082`epoch` of the previous or current default Version remain unchanged.
3083However, the Resource's `meta` sub-object's `modifiedat` and `epoch` attributes
3084MUST be updated.
3085
3086For clarity, when processing a request that results in
3087`defaultversionsticky` being `false`, then any existing `defaultversionid`
3088value, or value specified in the request, MUST be ignored for the purpose of
3089setting its final value.
3090
3091Any attempt to set `defaultversionid` to a non-existing Version, after all
3092Version processing for the current operation is completed, MUST generate an
3093error ([unknown_id](#unknown_id)).
3094
3095See [`defaultversionsticky` Attribute](#defaultversionsticky-attribute) below
3096for the relationship between these two attribute.
3097
3098See [Default Version of a Resource](#default-version-of-a-resource) for more
3099information about the management of default Versions.
3100
3101- Examples:
3102 - `1`, `2.0`, `v3-rc1` (v3's release candidate 1)
3103
3104#### `defaultversionurl` Attribute
3105- Type: URL
3106- Description: A URL to the default Version of the Resource.
3107
3108- API View Constraints:
3109 - REQUIRED.
3110 - MUST be an absolute URL to the default Version of the Resource, and MUST
3111 be the same as that Version's `self` attribute.
3112 - MUST be a read-only attribute.
3113 - If the Resource type's
3114 [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
3115 is set to `true`, then this URL MUST reference the xRegistry metadata view
3116 of the Version, not the domain-specific document view. In the HTTP
3117 protocol case, this means using the `$details` suffix.
3118
3119- Document View Constraints:
3120 - REQUIRED.
3121 - If the default Version is inlined in the document, then this attribute
3122 MUST be a relative URL of the form `#JSON-POINTER` where the `JSON-POINTER`
3123 locates the default Version within the current document. See
3124 [Doc Flag](#doc-flag) for more information.
3125 - If the default Version is not inlined in the document, then this attribute
3126 MUST be an absolute URL per the API view constraints listed above.
3127
3128- Examples:
3129 - `https://example.com/endpoints/ep1/messages/msg1/versions/1.0` (API View)
3130 - `#/endpoints/ep1/messages/msg1/versions/1.0` (Document View)
3131
3132#### `defaultversionsticky` Attribute
3133- Type: Boolean
3134- Description: A value of `true` means that `defaultversionid` has been
3135 explicitly set and its value MUST NOT automatically change if other Versions
3136 are added or removed. A value of `false` means the default Version MUST be
3137 the newest Version, as defined by the Resource's
3138 [`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) algorithm.
3139
3140- Constraints:
3141 - REQUIRED.
3142 - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.
3143 - When specified, it MUST be a case-sensitive `true` or `false`.
3144 - When specified in a request, a value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a
3145 request to delete the attribute, implicitly setting it to `false`.
3146 - When a Resource type's `maxversions` is set to `1`, any attempt to set
3147 this attribute to `true` MUST generate an error
3148 ([setdefaultversionsticky_false](#setdefaultversionsticky_false)) since
3149 setting a default/sticky Version is unnecessary when there can only be
3150 one Version.
3151
3152If a Resource type definition wishes to turn off the ability for clients to
3153select the "default" Version (or to set the `defaultversionsticky` attribute to
3154`true`), this MAY be done by modifying the definition of this attribute
3155in the Resource type's model. For example, in the `metaattributes` section
3156use the following definition:
3157
3158```yaml
3159"defaultversionsticky": {
3160 "name": "defaultversionsticky",
3161 "enum": [ false ],
3162 "required": true,
3163 "default": false
3164}
3165```
3166
3167Likewise, forcing all Resource instances to have "sticky" Versions MAY be
3168achieved via the same mechanism by using `true` instead of `false` in the
3169`enum` and `default` aspects.
3170
3171See [`defaultversionid` Attribute](#defaultversionid-attribute) for more
3172information on the relationship between these two attributes.
3173
3174See [Default Version of a Resource](#default-version-of-a-resource) for more
3175information about the management of default Versions.
3176
3177- Examples:
3178 - `true`, `false`
3179
3180### Version Entity
3181
3182Versions represent historical instances of a Resource. When a Resource is
3183updated, there are two actions that might take place. First, the update can
3184completely replace an existing Version of the Resource. This is most typically
3185done when the previous state of the Resource is no longer needed, and there
3186is no reason to allow people to reference it. The second situation is when
3187both the old and new Versions of a Resource are meaningful and both might need
3188to be referenced. In this case, the update will cause a new Version of the
3189Resource to be created and will have a unique `versionid` within the scope
3190of the Resource.
3191
3192For example, updating the data of Resource without creating a new Version
3193would make sense if there is an error in the `description` field. But, adding
3194additional data to the document of a Resource might require a new Version and
3195a new `versionid` (e.g. changing it from "1.0" to "1.1").
3196
3197This specification does not mandate a particular versioning algorithm or
3198Version identification (`versionid`) scheme.
3199
3200When a Version is serialized as xRegistry metadata it MUST adhere to the
3201following:
3202
3203```yaml
3204{
3205 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>", # <SINGULAR>id of Resource
3206 "versionid": "<STRING>",
3207 "self": "<URL>",
3208 "shortself": "<URL>", ?
3209 "xid": "<XID>",
3210 "epoch": <UINTEGER>,
3211 "name": "<STRING>", ?
3212 "isdefault": <BOOLEAN>,
3213 "description": "<STRING>", ?
3214 "documentation": "<URL>", ?
3215 "icon": "<URL>", ?
3216 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ?
3217 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
3218 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
3219 "ancestorid": "<STRING>",
3220 "contenttype": "<STRING>", ?
3221 "format": "<STRING>", ?
3222 "formatvalidated": <BOOLEAN>, ?
3223 "formatvalidatedreason": "<STRING>", ?
3224 "compatibilityvalidated": <BOOLEAN>, ?
3225 "compatibilityvalidatedreason": "<STRING>", ?
3226
3227 "<RESOURCE>url": "<URL>", ? # If not local
3228 "<RESOURCE>": ... Resource document ..., ? # If inlined & JSON
3229 "<RESOURCE>base64": "<STRING>" ? # If inlined & ~JSON
3230}
3231```
3232
3233Version extension attributes would also appear as additional top-level JSON
3234attributes.
3235
3236Versions include the following [common attributes](#common-attributes):
3237- [`<RESOURCE>id`](#singularid-id-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document
3238 views. OPTIONAL in requests. MUST be the `<RESOURCE>id` of the owning
3239 Resource.
3240- [`versionid`](#versionid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
3241 OPTIONAL in requests.
3242- [`self`](#self-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
3243 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. MUST be a URL to this Version, not the owning
3244 Resource.
3245- [`shortself`](#shortself-attribute) - OPTIONAL in API and document view,
3246 based on the `shortself` capability. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.
3247- [`xid`](#xid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
3248 OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. MUST be the `xid` of this Version, not the
3249 owning Resource.
3250- [`epoch`](#epoch-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL
3251 in requests. MUST be the `epoch` value of this Version, not the owning
3252 Resource.
3253- [`name`](#name-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
3254- [`description`](#description-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
3255- [`documentation`](#documentation-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
3256- [`icon`](#icon-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
3257- [`labels`](#labels-attribute) - OPTIONAL.
3258- [`createdat`](#createdat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
3259 OPTIONAL in requests.
3260- [`modifiedat`](#modifiedat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views.
3261 OPTIONAL in requests.
3262
3263and the following Version-level attributes:
3264
3265#### `versionid` Attribute
3266
3267- Type: String
3268- Description: An immutable unique identifier of the Version.
3269
3270- Constraints:
3271 - See [<SINGULAR>id](#singularid-id-attribute).
3272 - MUST be `<SINGULAR>id` of the Version.
3273 - REQUIRED in API and document views.
3274 - MUST NOT use a value of `null` or `request` due to these being reserved
3275 for use by the [SetDefaultVersionID Flag](#setdefaultversionid-flag).
3276 - If present in a request operation's serialization of a Resource's default
3277 Version attributes, then it MUST match the Resource's current
3278 `meta.defaultversionid` value (if defined), otherwise an error
3279 ([mismatched_id](./spec.md#mismatched_id)) MUST be generated.
3280
3281- Examples:
3282 - `1.0`
3283 - `v2`
3284 - `v3-rc`
3285
3286#### `isdefault` Attribute
3287- Type: Boolean
3288- Description: Indicates whether this Version is the "default" Version of the
3289 owning Resource.
3290
3291 See [Creating or Updating Resources and
3292 Versions](#creating-or-updating-resources-and-versions) for additional
3293 information about this attribute.
3294
3295- Constraints:
3296 - REQUIRED.
3297 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.
3298 - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.
3299 - When specified, MUST be either `true` or `false`, case-sensitive.
3300
3301- Examples:
3302 - `true`
3303 - `false`
3304
3305#### `ancestorid` Attribute
3306- Type: String
3307- Description: The `versionid` of this Version's ancestor.
3308
3309 The `ancestorid` attribute MUST be set to the case-sensitive `versionid` of
3310 this Version's ancestor. If this Version is a root of an ancestor hierarchy
3311 tree then it MUST be set to its own `versionid` value.
3312
3313 See the Resource's
3314 [`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) model
3315 aspect for more information on how this attribute value can be populated.
3316
3317 If a create operation asks the server to choose the `versionid` when
3318 creating a root Version, the `versionid` is not yet known and therefore
3319 cannot be specified in the `ancestorid` attribute as part of the request. In
3320 those cases a value of `request` MUST be used as a way to reference itself.
3321
3322- Constraints:
3323 - REQUIRED.
3324 - The `ancestorid` attribute MUST NOT be set to a value that
3325 creates circular references between Versions and it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED
3326 that the server generate an error
3327 ([ancestor_circular_reference](#ancestor_circular_reference)) if a request
3328 attempts to do so. For example, an operation that makes Version A's
3329 ancestor B, and Version B's ancestor A, would generate an error.
3330 - When absent in an update operation request, it MUST be interpreted as the
3331 same as if it were present with its existing value.
3332 - Any attempt to set an `ancestorid` attribute to a non-existing `versionid`
3333 MUST generate an error ([unknown_id](#unknown_id)).
3334 - Any modification to the `ancestorid` attribute MUST result in
3335 the owning Version's `epoch` and `modifiedat` attributes be updated
3336 appropriately, regardless of whether the change to `ancestorid` was
3337 explicitly part of a request or indirectly changed due to changes to other
3338 Versions.
3339
3340#### `contenttype` Attribute
3341- Type: String
3342- Description: The media type of the entity as defined by
3343 [RFC9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#media.type).
3344
3345- Constraints:
3346 - OPTIONAL.
3347 - SHOULD be compliant with
3348 [RFC9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#media.type).
3349 - This attribute MAY be specified even for Versions that use the
3350 `<RESOURCE>url` attribute. While this specification cannot guarantee that
3351 this attribute's value will match the media type value returned by a
3352 request to retrieve the document at the `<RESOURCE>url`, it is expected
3353 that they will match.
3354
3355- Examples:
3356 - `application/json`
3357
3358#### `format` Attribute
3359- Type: String
3360- Description: Identifies what the Version represents. For example, in the
3361 case of a Schema Registry, this value would identify the schema format of
3362 the Version's domain-specific document. However, it MAY also be used to
3363 identify the xRegistry metadata definitions/values for the Version. For
3364 example, it could be used to indicate that the Versions are
3365 [Message definitions](./../../message-v1/docs/spec.md).
3366
3367 Managers of the xRegistry instance MAY enforce validation of the data within
3368 the Registry by modifying the model to make this a mandatory attribute or
3369 by defining a default value.
3370
3371- Constraints:
3372 - OPTIONAL.
3373 - If present, MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string.
3374 - SHOULD follow the naming convention `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is
3375 the name of the format and `<VERSION>` is the version of the format used
3376 by this Version.
3377 - RECOMMENDED that the same `<NAME>` be used for all Versions of a Resource.
3378 - When not present, `format` validation MUST NOT be performed for that
3379 Version irrespective of the
3380 [`validateformat`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringvalidateformat)
3381 attribute's value.
3382
3383Note: an attempt to set this attribute to a value that differs from the other
3384Version's values could result in the server rejecting the request due to
3385the [`compatibility`](#compatibility-attribute) conformance checks, if
3386`validatecompatibility` model attribute is `true`.
3387
3388- Examples:
3389 - `JsonSchema/draft-07`
3390 - `Protobuf/3`
3391 - `XSD/1.1`
3392 - `Avro/1.9`
3393
3394#### `formatvalidated` Attribute
3395- Type: Boolean
3396- Description: When
3397 [`format` validation](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringvalidateformat)
3398 is enabled, this attribute will indicate whether or not the server has
3399 performed validation to ensure the Version conforms to the rules defined by
3400 its `format` attribute's value.
3401
3402 A value of `true` indicates that the server has validated the Version and
3403 it adheres to the `format` attribute's rules. When `true` the Version's
3404 [`formatvalidatedreason`](#formatvalidatedreason-attribute) MUST NOT be
3405 present.
3406
3407 A value of `false` indicates that the server did not perform validation of
3408 the Version. This can happen when
3409 [`strictvalidation`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)`
3410 is set to `false` and:
3411 - The `format` attribute value is not supported by the server.
3412 - The Version uses the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute to reference a
3413 domain-specific document stored outside of the Registry. In this case
3414 the server implementation doesn't have access to the document, and
3415 therefore can not verify it, nor does this specification mandate that it
3416 be able to access that URL.
3417
3418 When
3419 [`strictvalidation`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)`
3420 is `true`, the above conditions MUST generate an error
3421 ([format_unknown](#format_unknown) or [format_external](#format_external)) and
3422 reject the update request instead.
3423
3424 When `false`, the
3425 [`formatvalidatedreason`](#formatvalidatedreason-attribute)
3426 MUST be present with an explanation as to why the server was unable to
3427 perform validation of the Version. Additionally, when `false`, if
3428 `compatibility` validation is enabled, the Version's
3429 [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibility-attribute) attribute MUST also be
3430 `false`.
3431
3432 Note that `"false"` MUST NOT be used for validation failure. In those cases
3433 the write operation MUST generate an error
3434 ([format_violation](#format_violation)) and reject the request regardless
3435 of the value of the
3436 [`strictvalidation`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)`
3437 model aspect.
3438
3439- Constraints:
3440 - OPTIONAL
3441 - When specified, MUST be either `true` or `false`, case-sensitive.
3442 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.
3443 - MUST be present if the Resource model's `validateformat` attribute is
3444 `true` and the Version's `format` attribute is present.
3445 - MUST NOT be present if the Resource model's `validateformat` attribute is
3446 `false` or the Version's `format` attribute is absent.
3447
3448#### `formatvalidatedreason` Attribute
3449- Type: String
3450- Description: When [`formatvalidated`](#formatvalidated-attribute) has a
3451 value of `false`, this attribute MUST provide information as to why the
3452 format validation check was not performed.
3453
3454- Constraints:
3455 - OPTIONAL
3456 - When specified, MUST be a non-empty string.
3457 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.
3458 - MUST be present when [`formatvalidated`](#formatvalidated-attribute) is
3459 present with a value of `false`.
3460 - MUST NOT be present when [`formatvalidated`](#formatvalidated-attribute) is
3461 absent or has a value of `true`.
3462
3463#### `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute
3464- Type: Boolean
3465- Description: When [`compatibility`
3466 validation](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringvalidateformat)
3467 is enabled, this attribute will indicate whether or not the server has
3468 performed validation to ensure the Version conforms to the rules defined by
3469 its Resource's `meta.compatibility` attribute's value.
3470
3471 A value of `true` indicates that the server has validated the Version and
3472 it adheres to the `meta.compatibility` attribute's rules.
3473
3474 A value of `false` indicates that the server did not perform validation of
3475 the Version. This can happen when
3476 [`strictvalidation`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)`
3477 is set to `false` and:
3478 - The `formatvalidated` attribute is `false`.
3479 - The `format` or `meta.compatibility` attributes not supported by the
3480 server.
3481 - The Version uses the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute to reference a
3482 domain-specific document stored outside of the Registry. In this case
3483 the server implementation doesn't have access to the document, and
3484 therefore can not verify it, nor does this specification mandate that it
3485 be able to access that URL.
3486
3487 When
3488 [`strictvalidation`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)`
3489 is `true`, the above conditions MUST generate an error
3490 ([format_unknown](#format_unknown),
3491 [compatibility_unknown](#compatibility_unknown) or
3492 [format_external](#format_external)) and
3493 reject the update request instead.
3494
3495 When `false`, the
3496 [`compatibilityvalidatedreason`](#compatibilityvalidatedreason-attribute)
3497 MUST be present with an explanation as to why the server was unable to
3498 perform validation of the Version.
3499
3500 Note that `false` MUST NOT be used for validation failure. In those cases
3501 the write operation MUST generate an error
3502 ([compatibility_violation](#compatibility_violation)) and reject the request
3503 regardless of the value of the
3504 [`strictvalidation`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)`
3505 model aspect.
3506
3507- Constraints:
3508 - OPTIONAL
3509 - When specified, MUST be either `true` or `false`, case-sensitive.
3510 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.
3511 - MUST be present if the Resource model's `validatecompatibility` attribute
3512 is `true`, the Version's `format` value is present, and the Resource's
3513 `meta.compatibility` attribute is present.
3514 - MUST NOT be present if the Resource model's `validatecompatibility`
3515 attribute is `false`, or the Version's `format` value is absent, or the
3516 Resource's `meta.compatibility` attribute is absent.
3517
3518#### `compatibilityvalidatedreason` Attribute
3519- Type: String
3520- Description: When
3521 [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibilityvalidated-attribute) has a
3522 value of `false`, this attribute MUST provide information as to why the
3523 format validation check was not performed.
3524
3525- Constraints:
3526 - OPTIONAL
3527 - When specified, MUST be a non-empty string.
3528 - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.
3529 - MUST be present when
3530 [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibilityvalidated-attribute) is
3531 present with a value of `false`.
3532 - MUST NOT be present when
3533 [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibilityvalidated-attribute) is
3534 absent or has a value of `true`.
3535
3536#### `<RESOURCE>url` Attribute
3537- Type: URI
3538- Description: If the Version's domain-specific document is stored outside of
3539 the current Registry, then this attribute MUST contain a URL to the
3540 location where it can be retrieved. If the value of this attribute
3541 is a well-known identifier that is readily understood by Registry
3542 clients, and resolves to a common representation of the Version, or
3543 an item in some private store/cache, rather than a networked document
3544 location, then it is RECOMMENDED for the value to be a uniform resource
3545 name ([URN](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8141)).
3546
3547- Constraints:
3548 - REQUIRED if the Version's document is not stored inside of the current
3549 Registry.
3550 - If the document is stored in a network-accessible endpoint then the
3551 referenced URL MUST support a query to this URL to retrieve the contents.
3552 There is no requirement for the server to validate this URL.
3553 - MUST NOT be present if the Resource type's
3554 [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
3555 is set to `false`.
3556
3557#### `<RESOURCE>` Attribute
3558- Type: Resource Document
3559- Description: This attribute is a serialization of the corresponding
3560 Version's domain-specific document's contents. If the document's bytes
3561 "as is" (without any additional processing such as escaping) allows for
3562 them to appear as the value of this JSON attribute, then this attribute
3563 MUST be used if the request asked for the document to be
3564 [inlined](#inline-flag) in the response.
3565
3566 This is a convenience (optimization) attribute to make it easier to view the
3567 document when it happens to be in the same format as the serialization of
3568 the Version.
3569
3570 The model Resource attribute
3571 [`typemap`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringtypemap)
3572 MAY be used to help the server determine if the document is in the
3573 same format. If a Version has a matching `contenttype` attribute but the
3574 contents of the Version's document do not successfully parse (e.g. it's
3575 `application/json` but the JSON is invalid), then `<RESOURCE>`
3576 MUST NOT be used and `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be used instead.
3577
3578- Constraints
3579 - If the Version's document is to be serialized and is not empty,
3580 then either `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be present.
3581 - MUST only be used if the Version's document (bytes) is in the same
3582 format as the serialization of the Version entity.
3583 - MUST NOT be present if `<RESOURCE>base64` is also present.
3584 - MUST NOT be present if the Resource type's
3585 [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
3586 is set to `false`.
3587
3588#### `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute
3589- Type: String
3590- Description: This attribute is a base64 encoding of the corresponding
3591 Version's domain-specific document. If the Version's document (which is
3592 stored as an array of bytes) is not conformant with the format being used
3593 to serialize the Version (e.g. as a JSON value), then this attribute MUST be
3594 used instead of the `<RESOURCE>` attribute.
3595
3596- Constraints:
3597 - If the Version's document is to be serialized and it is not empty,
3598 then either `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be present.
3599 - If the Version's document is to be serialized but it is empty,
3600 then `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be present with an empty string (`""`) value.
3601 - MUST be a base64 encoded string of the Version's document.
3602 - MUST NOT be present if `<RESOURCE>` is also present.
3603 - MUST NOT be present if the Resource type's
3604 [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument)
3605 is set to `false`.
3606
3607---
3608
3609When accessing a Version's xRegistry metadata, often it is to
3610view or update the xRegistry metadata and not the document, as such, including
3611the potentially large amount of data from the Version's document in request
3612and response messages could be cumbersome. To address this, the `<RESOURCE>`
3613and `<RESOURCE>base64` attributes do not appear by default as part of the
3614serialization of the Version. Rather, they MUST only appear in responses when
3615the [Inline Flag](#inline-flag), with a value of `<RESOURCE>`, is used.
3616Likewise, in requests, these attributes are OPTIONAL and would only need to be
3617used when a change to the document's content is needed at the same time as
3618updates to the Version's metadata. However, the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute MUST
3619always appear if it has a value, just like any other attribute.
3620
3621Note that the serialization of a Version MUST only use at most one of these 3
3622attributes at a time.
3623
3624Client and server implementations MUST be prepared for any of these 3
3625attributes to be used. In the case of `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64`,
3626implementations can not assume that a previous use of one means that all
3627subsequent interactions with that entity will use the same attribute. For
