3628example, a client can use `<RESOURCE>` to populate the value, but the server
3629is free to use `<RESOURCE>base64` when returning the data.
3630
3631#### Version IDs
3632
3633If a server does not support client-side specification of the `versionid` of a
3634new Version (see the
3635[`setversionid` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringsetversionid)
3636in the [Registry Model](./model.md#registry-model)), or if a client chooses to
3637not specify the `versionid`, then the server MUST assign new Versions a
3638`versionid` that is unique within the scope of its owning Resource.
3639
3640Servers MAY have their own algorithm for the creation of new Version
3641`versionid` values, but the default algorithm is as follows:
3642- `versionid` MUST be a string serialization of a monotonically increasing
3643 (by `1`) unsigned integer starting with `1` and is scoped to the owning
3644 Resource.
3645- Each time a new `versionid` is needed, if an existing Version already has
3646 that `versionid` then the server MUST generate the next `versionid` value
3647 and try again.
3648- The search for the next value does not restart with `1` each time, it MUST
3649 continue from the highest previously generated value.
3650
3651With this default versioning algorithm, when semantic versioning is needed,
3652it is RECOMMENDED to include a major version identifier in the Resource
3653`<RESOURCE>id`, like `"com.example.event.v1"` or `"com.example.event.2024-02"`,
3654so that incompatible, but historically related Resources can be more easily
3655identified by users and developers. The Version's `versionid` then functions
3656as the semantic minor version identifier.
3657
3658#### Default Version of a Resource
3659
3660As Versions of a Resource are added or removed, there needs to be a mechanism
3661by which the "default" one is determined. There are two options for how this
3662might be done:
3663
36641. Default = Newest. The newest Version (based on the Resource's
3665 [`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode)
3666 algorithm) MUST become the "default" Version. This is the default choice.
3667
36681. Client explicitly chooses the "default". In this option, a client has
3669 explicitly chosen which Version is the "default" and it MUST NOT change
3670 until a client chooses another Version - this is referred to as the default
3671 Version being "sticky". When the current default Version is deleted and
3672 the client did not specify which Version is to become the next default
3673 Version (see below), then the server MUST revert back to option 1
3674 (default = newest).
3675
3676A client MAY choose the "default" Version two ways:
36771. Via the Resource
3678 [ `defaultversionsticky`](#defaultversionsticky-attribute) and
3679 [ `defaultversionid`](#defaultversionid-attribute) attributes
3680 in its `meta` sub-object.
36812. Via the
3682 [SetDefaultVersionID Flag](#setdefaultversionid-flag) that is available on
3683 certain APIs.
3684
3685See [`defaultversionid`](#defaultversionid-attribute) and
3686[`defaultversionsticky`](#defaultversionsticky-attribute) attributes for more
3687information.
3688
3689### Deleting Entities
3690
3691Each protocol binding will define how to delete entities, and in most cases
3692the operation will be straight-forward since the action will likely either
3693be a "delete" operation directed to the entity in question, or in the case
3694of deleting multiple entities, it will be directed to the owning collection
3695along with a map of entity IDs to be deleted.
3696
3697When deleting multiple entities, the list of entities to delete MUST be
3698specified as a map. There will be 3 possible ways in which the map will be
3699serialized:
3700
37011 - Deleting multiple entities (no `epoch` value checking)
3702
3703```yaml
3704{
3705 "<KEY>": {} # <SINGULAR>id of entity
3706} ?
3707```
3708
3709While this could have been represented as an array of IDs, for consistency
3710with the next two variants, and with what a query for the list of entities
3711in a collection will return, it's a map.
3712
37132 - Deleting multiple non-Resource entities with `epoch` value checking
3714
3715```yaml
3716{
3717 "<KEY>": { # <SINGULAR>id of entity
3718 "epoch": <UINTEGER> ?
3719 } *
3720} ?
3721```
3722
3723Since each entity has an `epoch` value associated with it, the server MUST
3724perform `epoch` value checking and reject the entire request if any fail. This
3725is similar to what an "update" operation would look like.
3726
37273 - Deleting multiple Resource entities with `epoch` value checking
3728
3729```yaml
3730{
3731 "<KEY>": { # <SINGULAR>id of Resource
3732 "meta": {
3733 "epoch": <UINTEGER> ?
3734 } ?
3735 } *
3736} ?
3737```
3738
3739Since a Resource's `epoch` value is part of its `meta` entity, and not a
3740top-level Resource attribute, for consistency with what the retrieval of
3741a Resource would look like, the `epoch` value in this case MUST appear under
3742a `meta` entity within the Resource. And then normal `epoch` value checking
3743rules would apply.
3744
3745This special serialization rules for Resources was done because an `epoch`
3746value that appears as a top-level attribute is likely done when a client
3747mistakenly uses a Version's serialization rather than the owning Resource's.
3748
3749If an `epoch` value only appears at the top-level (and not within `meta`) then
3750an error ([misplaced_epoch](./spec.md#misplaced_epoch)) MUST be generated.
3751If `epoch` appears in both places then the top-level one MUST be silently
3752ignored.
3753
3754---
3755
3756Regardless of type of "delete" being done, the following rules apply:
3757
3758- In the case of the "delete" being directed to a collection:
3759 - A map with no entities MUST NOT delete any entities.
3760 - Each key of the map MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of the entity to be deleted.
3761 - If the request body is absent (does not include a map), then all entities
3762 in the collection MUST be deleted.
3763 - If the entity's `<SINGULAR>id` is present in the request, then it MUST
3764 match its corresponding `<KEY>` value, otherwise a
3765 [mismatched_id](#mismatched_id) MUST be generated.
3766 - Any other entity attributes that appear in the request MUST be silently
3767 ignored, even if their values are invalid.
3768 - If one of the referenced entities cannot be found, then the server MUST
3769 silently ignore this condition and not treat it as an error.
3770- In the case of the "delete" being directed to a single entity:
3771 - If the entity cannot be found, then an error
3772 ([not_found](./spec.md#not_found)) MUST be generated.
3773- Deleting an entity MUST delete all children entities as well.
3774- Any error MUST result in the entire request being rejected.
3775
3776## Request Flags
3777
3778This specification allows for clients to configure server-side processing
3779via the use of "flags" (configuration options) on requests. The allowable
3780flags might vary based on the specific operation being performed, and some
3781will influence the processing of the request while some will influence the
3782how the response message will be generated.
3783
3784Implementations of this specification SHOULD support all
3785specification-defined flags.
3786
3787The following sections define each flag and then the protocol-specific
3788specifications will indicate how they are to be serialized on each request:
3789
3790- [`binary`](#binary-flag)
3791- [`collections`](#collections-flag)
3792- [`doc`](#doc-flag)
3793- [`epoch`](#epoch-flag)
3794- [`filter`](#filter-flag)
3795- [`ignore`](#ignore-flag)
3796- [`inline`](#inline-flag)
3797- [`setdefaultversionid`](#setdefaultversionid-flag)
3798- [`sort`](#sort-flag)
3799- [`specversion`](#specversion-flag)
3800
3801See: [Request Flags](./http.md#request-flags--query-parameters) in the
3802[HTTP binding specification](./http.md) for the HTTP usage.
3803
3804### Binary Flag
3805
3806The `binary` flag MAY be used on requests to indicate that the server MUST use
3807the `<RESOURCE>base64` attribute instead of the `<RESOURCE>` attribute when
3808serializing any Resource's domain-specific document in the response message.
3809 Note, the presence of this flag does not change when the document is inlined,
3810just how it is serialized if it is inlined.
3811
3812This flag is intended for cases where the client wishes to avoid the server
3813modifying the bytes of the document in any way - such as "pretty printing" it.
3814
3815This flag MAY be used on any request but will only influence the serialization
3816of Resource and Version entities that have a domain-specific document.
3817
3818### Collections Flag
3819
3820The `collections` flag MAY be used on requests directed to the Registry itself,
3821or to Group instances, to indicate that the response message MUST NOT include
3822any attributes from the top-level entity (Registry or Group), but instead MUST
3823include only all of the nested xRegistry Collection maps that are defined at
3824that level. Specifying it on a request directed to some other part of the
3825Registry MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)). Use of this flag MUST
3826implicitly turn on [inlining](#inline-flag) within a value of `*`.
3827
3828Servers MAY choose to include, or exclude, the sibling `<COLLECTION>url` and
3829`<COLLECTION>count` attributes for those top-level collections.
3830
3831Note that not including any of the attributes of an entity only applies to the
3832root entity of the response and not to any nested entities/collections.
3833
3834This feature is meant to be used when the Collections of the Registry, or
3835Group, are of interest but not the top-level metadata. For example, this could
3836be used to export one or more Group types from a Registry where the resulting
3837JSON document is then used to import them into another Registry. If the
3838Registry-level attributes were present in the output then they would need to
3839be removed prior to the import, otherwise they would override the target
3840Registry's values.
3841
3842For example, to export all of the Groups of one Registry into another, without
3843modifying the Registry entity's attributes, can be done via HTTP by taking the
3844results from:
3845
3846```yaml
3847GET http://sourceRegistry.com/?collections
3848```
3849
3850and using it as input into:
3851
3852```yaml
3853POST http://targetRegistry.com/
3854```
3855
3856### Doc Flag
3857
3858The `doc` flag MAY be used to indicate that the response MUST use "document
3859view" when serializing entities and MUST be modified to do the following:
3860- MUST remove the default Version attributes from a Resource's serialization.
3861- MUST remove the Version `formatvalidated` and `compatibilityvalidated`
3862 attributes from Version serializations.
3863- MUST remove the `shortself` attribute from all entity serializations.
3864- When a Resource (source) uses the `xref` feature, the target Resource's
3865 attributes MUST be excluded from the source's serialization.
3866- Resources and Versions MUST be serialized in their
3867 [xRegistry metadata view](#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) and not
3868 as any potential domain-specific document.
3869- MUST convert the following attributes into relative URLs if, and only if,
3870 the entities that they reference are included in the response output:
3871 `self`, `<COLLECTION>url`, `metaurl`, `defaultversionurl`.
3872
3873All of the relative URLs mentioned in the last bullet above MUST begin with `#`
3874and be followed by a
3875[JSON Pointer](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901) reference to the
3876entity within the response, e.g. `#/endpoints/e1`. This means that they are
3877relative to the root of the document (response) generated, and not necessarily
3878relative to the root of the Registry. Additionally, when those URLs are
3879relative and reference a Resource or Version, any protocol-specific
3880modifications to the URLs (e.g. the HTTP `$details` suffix) MUST NOT be
3881present despite the semantics of the suffix being applied (as noted below).
3882
3883For clarity, if a Registry has a Schema Resource at
3884`/schemagroups/g1/schemas/s1`, then this entity's `self` URL (when serialized
3885in document view) would change based on the path specified on the `GET`
3886request:
3887
3888| GET Path | `self` URL |
3889| --- | --- |
3890| `http://example.com/myreg` | `#/schemagroups/g1/schemas/s1` |
3891| `http://example.com/myreg/schemagroups` | `#/g1/schemas/s1` |
3892| `http://example.com/myreg/schemagroups/g1/ ` | `#/schemas/s1` |
3893| `http://example.com/myreg/schemagroups/g1/schemas ` | `#/s1` |
3894| `http://example.com/myreg/schemagroups/g1/schemas/s1` | `#/` |
3895
3896This feature is useful when a client wants to minimize the amount of data
3897returned by a server because the duplication of that data (typically used for
3898human readability purposes) isn't necessary. For example, if tooling would
3899ignore the duplication, or if the data will be used to populate a new
3900Registry, then this feature might be used. It also makes the output more of a
3901"stand-alone" document that minimizes external references.
3902
3903For clarity, the serialization of a Resource (when using `?inline=meta`) in
3904document view MUST adhere to the following:
3905
3906```yaml
3907{
3908 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>",
3909 "self": "<URL>",
3910 "xid": "<XID>",
3911
3912 "metaurl": "<URL>",
3913 "meta": {
3914 "<RESOURCE>id": "<STRING>",
3915 "self": "<URL>",
3916 "xid": "<XID>",
3917 "xref": "<XID>" ?
3918 # The following attributes are absent if 'xref' is set
3919 "epoch": <UINTEGER>,
3920 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ?
3921 "createdat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
3922 "modifiedat": "<TIMESTAMP>",
3923 "readonly": <BOOLEAN>,
3924 "compatibility": "<STRING>",
3925 "deprecated": { ... }, ?
3926
3927 "defaultversionid": "<STRING>",
3928 "defaultversionurl": "<URL>"
3929 "defaultversionsticky": <BOOLEAN> ?
3930 }
3931}
3932```
3933
3934Note that the `meta` entity's attributes `epoch` through
3935`defaultversionsticky` MUST be excluded if `xref` is set because those would
3936appear as part of the target Resource's `meta` entity. Also notice
3937the default Version's attributes do not appear.
3938
3939If this flag is used on a request directed to a Resource's `versions`
3940collection, or to one of its Versions, but the Resource is defined as an
3941`xref` to another Resource, then the server MUST generate an error
3942([cannot_doc_xref](#cannot_doc_xref)) and SHOULD indicate that using this
3943flag on this part of the hierarchy is not valid - due to those entities not
3944technically existing in document view.
3945
3946### Epoch Flag
3947
3948The `epoch` flag MAY be used on any delete operation directed to a single
3949entity if the protocol being used doesn't normally include the serialization
3950of the "to be deleted" entity in the request. In those cases, this flag is
3951used to request that the entity's current `epoch` value matches this flag's
3952value for the purpose of the server's
3953[`epoch` conflict checking algorithm](#epoch-attribute).
3954
3955### Filter Flag
3956
3957The `filter` flag MAY be used to indicate that the response MUST include only
3958those entities that match the specified filter criteria expressions. This
3959means that any Registry Collection's `<COLLECTION>*` attributes will be
3960modified to match the resulting subset. In particular:
3961- If the collection is inlined, it MUST only include entities that match the
3962 filter expression(s).
3963- The collection `url` attribute MAY include the appropriate filter
3964 expression(s) such that a query to that URL would return the same subset of
3965 entities, if the protocol supports including the filter flag value as part
3966 of the URL.
3967- The collection `count` attribute MUST only count the entities that match the
3968 filter expression(s).
3969
3970Parameters to this flag include one or more filter expressions. Each protocol
3971binding will indicate how to express logical ANDs and ORs between those
3972expressions. Regardless of how it is expressed the following rules apply:
3973- For expressions that are AND'd together, only entities that satisfy both
3974 expressions MUST be returned.
3975- For expressions that are OR'd together, only entities that satisfy either
3976 expression MUST be returned.
3977
3978The format of a filter expression is one of:
3979
3980```yaml
3981[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE>
3982[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE>=null
3983[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE>=[<VALUE>]
3984[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE><<VALUE>
3985[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE><=<VALUE>
3986[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE>><VALUE>
3987[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE>>=<VALUE>
3988[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE>!=<VALUE>
3989[<PATH>.]<ATTRIBUTE><><VALUE>
3990```
3991
3992Where:
3993- `<PATH>` MUST be an [xRegistry dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation)
3994 traversal of the Registry to the entity of interest, or absent if at the top
3995 of the Registry request.
3996- The `<PATH>` value MUST be based on the requesting URL and not the root of
3997 the Registry. Meaning, if the URL targets a Group then the `<PATH>` value
3998 would be relative to the Group and not the root of the Registry. See the
3999 examples below.
4000- `<ATTRIBUTE>` uses dot notation as well. Technically, the filter expression
4001 is a single dot notation reference, but the `<PATH>` and `<ATTRIBUTE>` are
4002 called out separately here for descriptive purposes.
4003- `<ATTRIBUTE>` MUST be the attribute in the entity to be examined.
4004- A non-`null` `<VALUE>` MUST only be used when referencing scalar attributes.
4005- A reference to a nonexistent attribute SHOULD NOT generate an error and
4006 SHOULD be treated the same as a non-matching situation. For example, a
4007 filter expression of `myobj.myattr=5` would not match if: `myobj` is missing,
4008 `myattr` is missing, or `myattr` is not `5`.
4009- The operators are processed as follows:
4010 - No operator:
4011 - When no operator is specified then the response MUST include
4012 all entities that have the `<ATTRIBUTE>` present with any non-`null`
4013 value.
4014 - `=` operator:
4015 - When `<VALUE>` is `null` then only entities without the specified
4016 `<ATTRIBUTE>` MUST be included in the response.
4017 - When a non-`null` `<VALUE>` is specified then `<VALUE>` MUST be the
4018 desired value of the attribute being examined. Only entities whose
4019 specified `<ATTRIBUTE>` with this `<VALUE>` MUST be included in the
4020 response.
4021 - When `<VALUE>` is absent then the implied `<VALUE>` is an empty string
4022 and the matching MUST be done as specified in the previous bullet.
4023 - `!=`, `<>` operators:
4024 - When `<VALUE>` is `null` then it MUST have the same semantics as a
4025 filter expression of `<ATTRIBUTE>` as specified above (meaning, present
4026 with any non-`null` value).
4027 - When `<VALUE>` is non-`null` then only entities without the specified
4028 `<ATTRIBUTE>` and `<VALUE>` MUST be included in the response. This MUST
4029 be semantically equivalent to `NOT(<ATTRIBUTE>=<VALUE>)`, and this also
4030 means that if `<ATTRIBUTE>` is missing then that attribute will match
4031 the filter.
4032 - `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` operators:
4033 - `<VALUE>` MUST NOT be `null`.
4034 - Only entities with the specified `<ATTRIBUTE>` and `<VALUE>` that matches
4035 the comparison operator's semantics MUST be included in the response.
4036 - `<` refers to "less than".
4037 - `<=` refers to "less than or equal to".
4038 - `>` refers to "greater than".
4039 - `>=` refers to "greater than or equal to".
4040
4041For comparing an `<ATTRIBUTE>` to the specified `<VALUE>`, and for purposes
4042of sorting (see the [Sort](#sort-flag) flag), the type of the attribute
4043impacts how the comparisons are done:
4044- For boolean attributes, comparisons MUST be an exact case-sensitive match
4045 (`true` or `false`). For relative comparisons, `false` is less than `true`.
4046- For numeric attributes, standard numeric comparisons rules apply. Note that
4047 numerics MUST NOT be treated as strings for comparison.
4048- For string attributes, the following rules apply:
4049 - The strings MUST be compared in a case-insensitive manner.
4050 - It is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED to use Unicode collation based on en-US.
4051 - See the next paragraph for information about use of wildcards.
4052- For timestamp attributes, after the values have been normalized to UTC,
4053 these follow the same rules as "strings" above.
4054- For URI/URL variants, these follow the same rules as "strings" above.
4055
4056See the [`Sort`](#sort-flag) section for more details concerning sorting.
4057
4058Additionally, wildcards (`*`) MAY be used in string `<VALUE>`s with the
4059following constraints:
4060- They MUST only be used when the comparison operator is `=`, `!=` or `<>`.
4061- The presence of a wildcard indicates that any number of characters MAY
4062 appear at that location in the `<VALUE>`.
4063- The wildcard MAY be escaped via the use of a backslash (`\\`) character
4064 (e.g. `abc\*def`) to mean that the `*` is to be interpreted as a normal
4065 character and not as a wildcard.
4066- A `<VALUE>` of `*` MUST be equivalent to checking for the existence of the
4067 attribute, with any value (even an empty string). In other words, the filter
4068 will only fail if the attribute has no value at all.
4069
4070As previously specified, when a query includes a filter expression, any nested
4071xRegistry collections in the response SHOULD result in the specification of a
4072`<COLLECTION>url` attribute that allows clients to easily traverse into that
4073collection with the appropriate sub-filter expression to yield the same
4074results as the original filter, but just for that nested collection. However,
4075if a collection has zero entities (regardless of whether the empty list is due
4076to the filter or due to the collection being empty), server MUST use a special
4077filter expression, `excludeall`, to indicate no results are to be returned for
4078that URL.
4079
4080For example, using HTTP:
4081```yaml
4082GET /?filter=schemagroups.schemas.name=myschema
4083
4084HTTP/1.1 200 OK
4085Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
4086
4087{
4088 ... Registry attributes excluded for brevity ...
4089 "messagegroupsurl": "http://example.com/messagegroups?filter=excludeall",
4090 "messagegroupscount": 0,
4091 "schemagroupsurl": "http://example.com/schemagroups?filter=schemas.name=myschema",
4092 "schemagroupscount": 10
4093}
4094```
4095
4096URLs with the `excludeall` filter expression MUST adhere to the following:
4097- If the URL references a collection then an empty collection (`{}`) MUST be
4098 returned.
4099- If the URL references an entity, then an error ([not_found](#not_found)) MUST
4100 be generated.
4101- If any other filter expression appears at the same time, then an error
4102 ([bad_filter](#bad_filter)) MUST be generated.
4103- This value is expected to only be used by servers in response to a query that
4104 used a filter and produces a `<COLLECTION>url` to an empty collection.
4105
4106If the request references an entity (not a collection), and the filter
4107expression references an attribute in that entity (i.e. there is no `<PATH>`),
4108then if the expression does not match the entity, that entity MUST NOT be
4109returned. In other words, a `404 Not Found` would be generated in the HTTP
4110protocol case.
4111
4112Invalid filter expressions MUST generate an error ([bad_filter](#bad_filter)).
4113
4114**Examples:**
4115
4116Using the [HTTP protocol binding](./http.md) syntax:
4117
4118| Request Path | Filter query | Commentary |
4119| --- | --- | --- |
4120| / | `?filter=endpoints.description=*cool*` | Only endpoints with the word `cool` in the description |
4121| /endpoints | `?filter=description=*CooL*` | Similar results as previous, with a different request URL |
4122| / | `?filter=endpoints.messages.versions.versionid=1.0` | Only versions (and their owning parents) that have a `versionid` of `1.0` |
4123| / | `?filter=endpoints.name=myendpoint,endpoints.description=*cool*& filter=schemagroups.labels.stage=dev` | Only endpoints whose name is `myendpoint` and whose description contains the word `cool`, as well as any schemagroups with a `label` name/value pair of `stage/dev` |
4124| / | `?filter=description=no-match` | Returns a 404 if the Registry's `description` doesn't equal `no-match` |
4125| / | `?filter=endpoints.messages.meta.readonly=true` | Only messages that are `readonly` |
4126
4127Specifying a filter does not imply inlining. Inlining MAY be used at
4128the same time but MUST NOT result in additional entities being included in
4129the results unless they are children of a matching leaf entity.
4130
4131For example, in the following entity URL paths representing a Registry:
4132
4133```yaml
4134mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v1
4135mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v2
4136mygroups/g1/myresources/r2/versions/v1
4137mygroups/g2/myresources/r3/versions/v1
4138```
4139
4140This HTTP request:
4141```yaml
4142GET /?filter=mygroups.myresources.myresourceid=r1&inline=*
4143```
4144
4145would result in the following entities (and their parents along the specified
4146paths) being returned:
4147
4148```yaml
4149mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v1 # versions are due to inlining
4150mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v2
4151```
4152
4153However, this request:
4154
4155```yaml
4156GET /?filter=mygroups.mygroupid=g2&filter=mygroups.myresources.myresourceid=r1&inline=*
4157```
4158
4159would result in the following returned:
4160
4161```yaml
4162mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v1 # from 2nd ?filter
4163mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v2 # from 2nd ?filter
4164mygroups/g2/myresources/r3/versions/v1 # from 1nd ?filter
4165```
4166
4167And, this request:
4168
4169```yaml
4170GET /?filter=mygroups.mygroupid=g1&filter=mygroups.myresources.myresourceid=r1&inline=*
4171```
4172
4173would result in the following being returned:
4174
4175```yaml
4176mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v1 # from 2nd ?filter
4177mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v2 # from 2nd ?filter
4178mygroups/g1/myresources/r2/versions/v1 # from 1st ?filter
4179```
4180
4181And, finally this request:
4182
4183```yaml
4184GET /?filter=mygroups.mygroupid=g1,mygroups.myresources.myresourceid=r1&inline=*
4185```
4186
4187would result in the following being returned:
4188
4189```yaml
4190mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v1
4191mygroups/g1/myresources/r1/versions/v2
4192```
4193
4194Notice the first part of the filter expression (to the left of the "and"
4195(`,`)) has no impact on the results because the list of resulting leaves in
4196that subtree is not changed by that search criteria.
4197
4198### Ignore Flag
4199
4200The `ignore` flag MAY be used on any write operation to indicate that certain
4201parts of the request message MUST be ignored by the server. This flag is
4202designed for cases where a user wants to import data into a Registry without
4203going through the (potentially tedious) process of removing certain parts of
4204the data in advance. Typically, in an "export->import" scenario.
4205
4206This flag takes a list of strings indicating which aspects of the request
4207message to ignore. This specification defines the following values:
4208
4209- `capabilities`
4210
4211 This value indicates that any `capabilities` attribute included in the
4212 request MUST be ignored.
4213
4214- `defaultversionid`
4215
4216 This value indicates that any `defaultversionid` attribute included in the
4217 request MUST be ignored.
4218
4219- `defaultversionsticky`
4220
4221 This value indicates that any `defaultversionsticky` attribute included in
4222 the request MUST be ignored.
4223
4224- `epoch`
4225
4226 This value indicates that any `epoch` attribute included in the request MUST
4227 be ignored.
4228
4229- `id`
4230
4231 When this value is used then any `<SINGULAR>id` present in the root entity
4232 MUST be ignored, and any validation to ensure it matches the targeted
4233 entity's existing `<SINGULAR>id` value MUST NOT be performed.
4234
4235 This feature MUST only apply in cases where the request is targeted to a
4236 single entity not a collection.
4237
4238 This feature is designed for cases where an entity is exported and then used
4239 as input for another entity where that targeted entity needs to use a
4240 different `<SINGULAR>id` for the root entity, without needing to transform
4241 the exported data.
4242
4243 Note that any nested entities in the request MUST retain their `<SINGULAR>id`
4244 values.
4245
4246 In cases where the target entity is a Version, then the flag MUST apply to
4247 both the Resource's `<SINGULAR>id` and the `versionid`.
4248
4249- `modelsource`
4250
4251 This value indicates that any `modelsource` attribute included in the request
4252 MUST be ignored.
4253
4254- `readonly`
4255
4256 This value indicates that any attempt to modify a read-only Resource MUST be
4257 silently ignored as if the Resource in question was never included in the
4258 request. Usage of this value in situations where removing the Resource from
4259 the request would invalidate the syntax or semantics of the request MUST
4260 generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).
4261
4262 To clarify its usage consider the following scenarios:
4263 - An update or delete request with `ignore` set to `readonly` directed to an
4264 individual read-only Resource would generate an error because removing
4265 the Resource from the request invalidates the validity of the request.
4266 - An update or delete request with `ignore` set to `readonly` directed to a
4267 Resource collection would ignore the read-only Resources referenced in the
4268 collection map (conceptually removing them from the request), and the
4269 request would still be valid (syntactically and semantically), even if the
4270 resulting map is empty. The request would not generate an error due to the
4271 usage of this flag.
4272
4273Implementations MAY define additional values.
4274
4275Specifying the flag without any values, an empty string, or `*` indicates a
4276request to ignore all possible (server supported) aspects of the request
4277message.
4278
4279Specifying an invalid, or unsupported, value for this flag MUST generate an
4280error ([bad_ignore](#bad_ignore)).
4281
4282### Inline Flag
4283
4284The `inline` flag MAY be used on requests to indicate whether nested
4285collections/objects, or certain (potentially large) attributes, are to be
4286included in the response message.
4287
4288The `inline` flag on a request indicates that the response MUST include the
4289contents of all specified inlineable attributes. Inlineable attributes include:
4290- The `model` attribute on the Registry entity.
4291- The `modelsource` attribute on the Registry entity.
4292- The `capabilities` attribute on the Registry entity.
4293- All [Registry Collection](#registry-collections) types - e.g. `<GROUPS>`,
4294 `<RESOURCES>` and `versions`.
4295- The `<RESOURCE>` attribute in a Resource or Version.
4296- The `meta` attribute in a Resource.
4297
4298Specifying the name of a non-inlineable attribute MUST generate an error
4299([inline_noninlineable](#inline_noninlineable)).
4300
4301While the `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCE>base64` attributes are defined as two
4302separate attributes, they are technically two separate "views" of the same
4303underlying data. As such, the usage of each will be based on the content type
4304of the Resource, and specifying `<RESOURCE>` in the `inline` flag value
4305MUST be interpreted as a request for the appropriate attribute. In other words,
4306`<RESOURCE>base64` is not a valid `inline` value.
4307
4308Use of this feature is useful for cases where the contents of the Registry are
4309to be represented as a single (self-contained) document.
4310
4311Some examples using the [HTTP protocol binding](./http.md#inline-flag):
4312- `GET /?inline=model` # Just 'model'
4313- `GET /?inline=model,endpoints` # Model and one level under `endpoints`
4314- `GET /?inline=*` # Everything except 'model','modelsource','capabilities'
4315- `GET /?inline=model,*` # Everything, including 'model'
4316- `GET /?inline=endpoints.messages` # One level below 'endpoints.messages'
4317- `GET /?inline=endpoints.*` # Everything below 'endpoints'
4318- `GET /endpoints/ep1/?inline=messages.message` # Just 'message'
4319- `GET /endpoints/ep1/messages/msg1?inline=message` # Just 'message'
4320
4321The value of the `inline` flag is a list of `<PATH>` values where each is a
4322string indicating which inlineable attribute to show in the response.
4323References to nested attributes are represented using an
4324[xRegistry dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation) where the xRegistry
4325collection names along the hierarchy are concatenated. For example:
4326`endpoints.messages.versions` will inline all Versions of Messages. Non-leaf
4327parts of the `<PATH>` MUST only reference xRegistry collection names and not
4328any specific entity IDs since `<PATH>` is meant to be an abstract traversal of
4329the model.
4330
4331There MAY be multiple `<PATH>`s specified in a single request and each
4332protocol binding specification will indicate how the list is specified.
4333
4334The `*` value MAY be used to indicate that all nested inlineable attributes
4335at that level in the hierarchy (and below) MUST be inlined - except `model`,
4336`modelsource` and `capabilities` at the root of the Registry. These three are
4337excluded since the data associated with them are configuration related. To
4338include their data the request MUST include `<PATH>` values of `model`,
4339`modelsource` or `capabilities` explicitly. Use of `*` MUST only be used as
4340the last part of the `<PATH>` (in its entirety). For example, `foo*` and
4341`*.foo` are not valid `<PATH>` values, but `*` and `endpoints.*` are.
4342
4343An `inline` flag without any value MAY be supported and if so it MUST have the
4344same semantic meaning as a value of `*`.
4345
4346The specific value of `<PATH>` will vary based on where the request is
4347directed. For example, a request to the root of the Registry MUST start with a
4348`<GROUPS>` name, while a request directed at a Group would start with a
4349`<RESOURCES>` name.
4350
4351For example, given a Registry with a model that has `endpoints` as a Group and
4352`messages` as a Resource within `endpoints`, the table below shows some
4353`<PATH>` values and a description of the result for the HTTP protocol:
4354
4355| HTTP `GET` Path | Example `?inline=<PATH>` values | Comment |
4356| --- | --- | --- |
4357| / | ?inline=endpoints | Inlines the `endpoints` collection, but just one level of it, not any nested inlineable attributes |
4358| / | ?inline=endpoints.messages.versions | Inlines the `versions` collection of all messages. Note that this implicitly means the parent entities (`messages` and `endpoints` would also be inlined - however any other `<GROUPS>` or `<RESOURCES>`s types would not be |
4359| /endpoints | ?inline=messages | Inlines just `messages` and not any nested attributes. Note we don't need to specify the parent `<GROUP>` since the URL already included it |
4360| /endpoints/ep1 | ?inline=messages.versions | Similar to the previous `endpoints.messages.version` example |
4361| /endpoints/ep1 | ?inline=messages.message | Inline the Resource document |
4362| /endpoints/ep1 | ?inline=endpoints | Invalid, already in `endpoints` and there is no `<RESOURCES>` called `endpoints` |
4363| / | ?inline=endpoints.messages.meta | Inlines the `meta` entity of each `message` returned. |
4364| / | ?inline=endpoints.* | Inlines everything for all `endpoints`. |
4365
4366Note that asking for an attribute to be inlined will implicitly cause all of
4367its parents to be inlined as well, but just the parent's collections needed to
4368show the child. In other words, just the collection in the parent in which the
4369child appears, not all collections in the parent.
4370
4371When specifying a collection to be inlined, it MUST be specified using the
4372plural name for the collection in its defined case.
4373
4374A request to inline an unknown, or non-inlineable, attribute MUST generate an
4375error ([bad_inline](#bad_inline)).
4376
4377Note: If the Registry cannot return all expected data in one response because
4378it is too large then it MUST generate an error ([too_large](#too_large)). In
4379those cases, the client will need to query the individual inlineable
4380collection attributes in isolation so the Registry can leverage a pagination
4381type of feature to iteratively retrieve the entities.
4382
4383### SetDefaultVersionID Flag
4384
4385The `setdefaultversionid` flag MAY be used on any write operation directed to
4386a single Resource, its `meta` sub-object or its Versions. The primary use case
4387is one in which the current default Version is being deleted and the client
4388wishes to choose a new default Version at the same time - to avoid an incorrect
4389one being chosen temporarily.
4390
4391Use of this flag on an operation that allows for modifying multiple Resources
4392MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).
4393
4394This flag MUST include a single parameter, a string containing the
4395case-sensitive `versionid` of the Version that is to become the new default
4396Version.
4397
4398The following rules apply:
4399- A value of `null` indicates that the client wishes to switch to the
4400 ["default = newest" algorithm](#default-version-of-a-resource). In other
4401 words, the "sticky" aspect of the current default Version will be removed
4402 and `meta.defaultversionsticky` MUST be set to `false`.
4403- If during a Version create operation the server is asked to choose the
4404 `versionid` value for the new Version, then including that value as the
4405 `setdefaultversionid` value is not possible. In those cases a value of
4406 `request` MAY be used as a way to reference that new Version.
4407- A value of `request` MUST only be used on APIs that allow the creation of
4408 only a single new Version. In the case of HTTP, that is the `POST` API
4409 directed to a Resource. This is because no other operation allows for the
4410 creation of a single Version without specifying its `versionid`. Using it
4411 when more than one Version is created MUST generate an error
4412 ([too_many_versions](#too_many_versions)). Other uses of this value on an
4413 inappropriate API MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).
4414- If a value of `request` was used but no Version was created for the request,
4415 then an error ([defaultversionid_request](#defaultversionid_request)) MUST
4416 be generated.
4417- If a non-`null` and non-`request` value does not reference an existing
4418 Version of the Resource, after all Version processing is completed, then an
4419 error ([unknown_id](#unknown_id)) MUST be generated.
4420- Setting the `meta.defaultversionid` to a non-empty value via this flag MUST
4421 also set the `meta.defaultversionsticky` attribute to `true`.
4422- Use on a request that updates more than one Resource MUST generate an
4423 error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).
4424- Use of this flag MUST override any `meta.defaultversionid` and
4425 `meta.defaultversionsticky` values that are present in the request.
4426
4427Any other invalid usage of this flag MUST generate an error
4428([bad_defaultversionid](#bad_defaultversionid)).
4429
4430### Sort Flag
4431
4432When a request is directed to a collection of Groups, Resources or Versions,
4433the `Sort` flag MAY be used to indicate the order in which the entities of
4434that collection are to be returned (i.e. sorted). Use of the `sort` flag
4435on a non-collection result MUST generate an error
4436([sort_noncollection](#sort_noncollection)).
4437
4438This flag MUST include a single parameter, a string containing the attribute
4439(`<ATTRIBUTE>`) name to use as the "sort key" plus an OPTIONAL indication of
4440 whether the results are to be sorted in ascending or descending order.
4441
4442The following rules apply:
4443- `<ATTRIBUTE>` MUST be a [dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation) path
4444 to one of the attributes defined in collection's entities that will be the
4445 primary sort key for the results.
4446 The attribute MUST only reference a scalar attribute within the top-level
4447 collection, it MUST NOT attempt to traverse into a nested xRegistry
4448 collection even if that nested collection is inlined.
4449- An OPTIONAL "sort order" (`asc` for ascending, `desc` for descending) MAY
4450 be specified to indicate whether the first entity in the returned collection
4451 MUST be the "lowest" values (`asc`) or whether it MUST be the "highest"
4452 value (`desc`). When not specified, the default value MUST be `asc`.
4453
4454When a pagination type of feature is used to return the results, but
4455the `sort` flag is not specified, then the server MUST sort the results on the
4456entities' `<SINGULAR>id` value in ascending order. When pagination is not used,
4457it is RECOMMENDED that servers still sort the results by `<SINGULAR>id` (asc)
4458for consistency.
4459
4460Sorting MUST be done using the data type comparison rules as specified in the
4461[filter Flag](#filter-flag) section. However, there are certain situations
4462that might introduce ambiguity between implementations. For example, not all
4463persistent stores support `NaNs` (Not-a-Number values), or if the data type of
4464an attribute changes on a per-instance basis, then consistent sorting across
4465implementations on that attribute might be challenging. While interoperability
4466is critical, requiring consistency in these edge cases could be excessively
4467burdensome for implementations. To that end, this specification does not
4468mandate the exact ordering in these situations, aside from the requirement
4469that an implementation MUST sort the result the same way each time.
4470
4471Entities that do not have a value for the specified attribute MUST be treated
4472the same as if they had the "lowest" possible value for that attribute. If
4473more than one entity shares the same attribute value then the `<SINGULAR>id`
4474MUST be used as a secondary sorting key, using the same `asc`/`desc` value
4475specified for the primary sorting key.
4476
4477An invalid usage of, or value for, the `sort` flag MUST generate an error
4478([bad_sort](#bad_sort)).
4479
4480Some examples using the [HTTP protocol binding](./http.md#sort-flag):
4481- `GET /endpoints?sort=name` # Sort (asc) on 'name', then 'endpointid'
4482- `GET /endpoints/e1/messages?sort=messageid=desc` # Sort (desc) on 'messageid'
4483- `GET /endpoints?sort=labels.stage` # Sort (asc) on `labels.stage`, then `endpointid`
4484
4485### SpecVersion Flag
4486
4487The SpecVersion flag MAY be used to indicate the xRegistry specification
4488version that the response MUST adhere to. The parameter value of this flag
4489MUST be a case-insensitive string.
4490
4491If the specified version is not supported, then an error
4492([unsupported_specversion](#unsupported_specversion)) MUST be generated.
4493When not specified, the default value MUST be the newest version of this
4494specification supported by the server.
4495
4496When comparing `specversion` strings, the server MUST silently ignore the
4497"patch" version number and only consider the "major.minor" version numbers.
4498This is because any "patch" version updates will only contain clarifications
4499and ought not require any code changes for server implementations. Therefore,
4500all patch versions of the same "major.minor" version MUST be forwards and
4501backwards compatible.
4502
4503However, due to the potential for semantics changes of versions with suffix
4504values (e.g. `v2.0.0-rc1`), the suffix value MUST be part of the comparison
4505checking.
4506
4507## xRegistry Dot (`.`) Notation
4508
4509This specification defines a syntax for referencing entities and attributes
4510within the xRegistry metadata. Known as "dot notation", it borrows some
4511of the core aspects of the [JSON Path](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9535)
4512specification.
4513
4514The following notation operators are defined:
4515
4516- `.NAME` : access a property (or key) of an object (or map).
4517- `['NAME']` : same as previous but `NAME` contains characters that are not
4518 to be interpreted as an operator (e.g. `.`) or it contains just digits and
4519 is not to be interpreted as an array index.
4520- `["NAME"]` : same as previous but with double-quotes (`"`).
4521- `[INTEGER]` : access an array index (zero-based).
4522
4523Note: due to the serialization of maps and objects (often) being
4524indistinguishable, this specification (similar to JSONPath) does not provide
4525different syntaxes for traversing each.
4526
4527For clarity, use of square brackets (`[]`) without use of either type of
4528quotes around the value MUST be interpreted as accessing an array. Conversely,
4529use of quotes MUST be interpreted as accessing an object/map.
4530
4531**Examples:**
4532
4533| Dot Notation | Description |
4534| ----------------- | --- |
4535| `.name` | An attribute (or map key) called `name` |
4536| `['my.name']` | An attribute (or map key) called `my.name` |
4537| `[2]` | The 3rd (zero-based) item in an array |
4538| `["birth.date"] ` | Attribute/key called `birth.date` |
4539| `["2"]` | An attribute/key called `2` (a string, not integer)|
4540| `employee.name` | `name` attribute/key in an object/map called `employee` |
4541| `stack[3]` | Element with index 3 (zero-based) in `stack` array |
4542| `employee['joe'].addresses[0].state` | `joe` attr/key of `employee`, then the first index of its `addresses` array, then `state` attr/key of that address |
4543
4544Depending on the situation in which the notation is being used, there are
4545certain special values that MAY be used, as described in the following sections.
4546
4547### Dot-Notation in Filters
4548
4549When using [filters](#filter-flag) the following special values MAY be used:
4550| | |
4551| ------ | --- |
4552| `.*` | Match any item in an object/map |
4553| `[*]` | Match any item in an array |
4554
4555Note that `['*']` is not the same as `.*`. Rather, `['*']` is a reference
4556to an attribute/key called `*` - assuming that it is a valid attribute/key
4557name in that particular situation.
4558
4559**Examples**
4560
4561Given the following definition of a `schemagroup` Group type extension:
4562
4563```yaml
4564{
4565 "info": {
4566 "owner": <STRING>,
4567 "reviewers": [ <STRING>, * ] # An array of strings
4568 "labels": { "<STRING>": "<STRING>" * }, ? # A map of string -> string
4569 "addresses": {
4570 "<STRING>": { # e.g. "home", "work"
4571 "street": "<STRING>",
4572 "state": "<STRING>",
4573 "zip": "<STRING>"
4574 } *
4575 } *
4576 },
4577 "age": <INTEGER>
4578}
4579```
4580
4581- Find all schemagroups that have an `age` of `5`:
4582 `GET /?filter=schemagroups.age=5`
4583- Find all schemagroups where `owner` is `joe`:
4584 `GET /?filter=schemagroups.info.owner=joe`
4585- Find all schemagroups that have a label `env` set to `prod`:
4586 `GET /?filter=schemagroups.info.labels.env=prod`
4587- Find all schemagroups that have any label with a value of `June`:
4588 `GET /?filter=schemagroups.info.labels.*=June`
4589- Find all schemagroups that have a "reviewers" value of `Steve`:
4590 `GET /?filter=schemagroups.info.reviewers[*]=Steve`
4591- Find all schemagroups that have an "info.address" in `CA`:
4592 `GET /?filter=schemagroups.info.addresses.*.state=CA`
4593
4594In the above examples, notice that the filter only specified the `schemagroups`
4595collection as part of the hierarchy traversal. From a purist perspective those
4596filters really ought to have been written with the `*` wildcard for the
4597matching schemagroups's `ID`, for example:
4598
4599```yaml
4600?filter=schemagroups.*.info.owner
4601```
4602
4603to indicate that we're asking to search over all schemagroups (by ID) in the
4604`schemagroups` collection, and then for each one examine its `info.owner`
4605attribute. However, requiring that extra bit of information in the filter
4606would introduce two potential problems:
4607
4608- It would mandate all users add `.*.` in almost all filter expressions,
4609 which could be tedious since in most cases it's expected that people are
4610 going to search over all items in the xRegistry collection.
4611- Additionally, if they were interested in just one item in the collection,
4612 then they would most likely have specified that as part of the request URL.
4613 For example, `GET /schemagroups/mygroup/...` - in which case the ID would
4614 not appear as part of the filter expression at all.
4615
4616As a result, when specifying a filter expression that steps between the
4617xRegistry hierarchy, the `ID` portion of the path is excluded. However, this
4618does not apply to stepping through the path of objects/maps/arrays defined
4619within an xRegistry entity (Group, Resource, Versions). In those cases use
4620of the `*` wildcard would need to be used to indicate "any" items in that set.
4621This is demonstrated in the "info.addresses" example above.
4622
4623For completeness, to filter based on a schema's name, the request might
4624look like:
4625
4626```yaml
4627GET /?filter=schemagroups.schemas.name=myschema
4628```
4629
4630would search over all schemagroups, and over all schemas in those groups,
4631for ones with a `name` attribute set to `myschema`.
4632
4633It is worth noting that if the user really does want a certain schemagroup with
4634a certain ID (e.g. `mygroup`), without the request URL path being
4635`/schemagroups/mygroup`, then they can achieve this by using a compound
4636filter:
4637
4638```yaml
4639GET /?filter=schemagroups.schemas.name=myschema,schemagroups.schemagroupid=mygroup
4640```
4641
4642The `,` in a single filter expression represents an `AND` operation.
4643
4644### Additional Special Dot-Notation Considerations
4645
4646The dot-notation defined in this specification is purposely limited to keep
4647implementation requirements to a minimum. However, third-party xRegistry
4648tooling might leverage more expressive dot-notation features. In order to
4649encourage interoperability and consistency across tooling, the following
4650syntax guidelines are RECOMMENDED for other common situations:
4651
4652- Insert an item into the middle of an array: `[INTEGER:]`.
4653 - E.g. `set myarray[3:]=mary` would be used to insert "mary" at the 4th
4654 index (zero-based), pushing current index positions 3 (and higher) further
4655 down in the array.
4656 - If the specified integer value does not exist, then an error is generated.
4657 Even in the case of `0` for an empty array.
4658- Insert at the start of an array: `[^]`.
4659 - E.g. `set myarray[^]=mary` would insert "mary" at the start of the array,
4660 and create the array first if it is not yet defined.
4661- Append to the end of an array: `[$]`.
4662 - E.g. `set myarray[$]=mary` would append "mary" to the end of the array,
4663 and create the array first if it is not yet defined.
4664- Referencing the last item in an array: `[-1]`.
4665 - E.g. `set myarray[-1]=mary` would replace the last item in the array.
4666 - If the array is empty, then an error is generated.
4667 - This notation does not extend to other negative integers.
4668- Specifying an empty object/map: `{}`.
4669 - E.g. `set myobject={}` would replace any value for `myobject` with an
4670 empty object/map.
4671- Specifying an empty array: `[]`.
4672 - E.g. `set myarray=[]` would replace any values in `myarray` with an empty
4673 array.
4674- Deleting an item from an array would shift all higher indexed items down one
4675 since this specification does not support sparse arrays. Note, that if the
4676 intent is to replace that item, rather than doing a delete followed by an
4677 insert, a direct replacement of that index is suggested.
4678
4679## xRegistry Discovery
4680
4681This specification defines the following mechanisms by which xRegistry servers
4682can be discovered:
4683
4684### Host-based Discovery
4685
4686If access to the root of a hosting environment is available, then it is
4687RECOMMENDED that implementations leverage the
4688[`/.well-known` discovery
4689mechanism](https://www.iana.org/assignments/well-known-uris/well-known-uris.xhtml)
4690by making xRegistry "discovery" metadata available at the
4691following URL:
4692
4693```yaml
4694/.well-known/xregistry
4695```
4696
4697If supported, a request (`GET`) to this location MUST return a document of
4698the form:
4699
4700```yaml
4701{
4702 "registries": [
4703 "URL", *
4704 ]
4705}
4706```
4707
4708Where:
4709- Each `URL` is the full absolute URL location an xRegistry server.
4710
4711While normally this list would only include xRegistry servers hosted on this
4712specific host, it is not a requirement that this be the case.
4713
4714- Examples:
4715 - ```yaml
4716 {
4717 "registries": [
4718 "https://example.com/schemaregistry"
4719 ]
4720 }
4721 ```
4722
4723### Registry-base Discovery
4724
4725Similar to the [Host-based Discovery](#host-based-discovery) mechanism,
4726an xRegistry server instance MAY advertise a list of additional xRegistry
4727servers by supporting a protocol-specific retrieval mechanism.
4728
4729Regardless of the exact protocol mechanism, the data returned MUST adhere
4730to the same format as the Host-based discovery mechanism:
4731
4732```yaml
4733{
4734 "registries": [
4735 "URL", *
4736 ]
4737}
4738```
4739
4740Where:
4741- Each `URL` is the full absolute URL location an xRegistry server.
4742- While not expected, the list MAY include the current server's URL.
4743- This list MAY, but is not mandated to, include URLs from the
4744 host-based discovery mechanism. It is expected that clients will
4745 detect duplicate URLs if needed.
4746
4747See the [xRegistry HTTP specification](./http.md#xregistry-discovery) for more
4748information on the HTTP-specific discovery mechanism.
4749
4750- Examples:
4751 - Using HTTP, a "dev" registry, points to a "prod" registry:
4752 ```yaml
4753 GET http://example.com/registries/dev/.xregistry
4754
4755 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
4756 Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
4757
4758 {
4759 "registries": [
4760 "https://example.com/registries/prod"
4761 ]
4762 }
4763 ```
4764 - Additionally, if access to the root of the host is available, the
4765 following would work:
4766 ```yaml
4767 GET http://example.com/.well-known/xregistry
4768
4769 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
4770 Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
4771
4772 {
4773 "registries": [
4774 "https://example.com/registries/dev",
4775 "https://example.com/registries/prod"
4776 ]
4777 }
4778 ```
4779
4780Since clients might not be aware of the hosting limitations of the servers,
4781to maximize the set of xRegistries servers found, both Host-based and
4782Registry-based mechanisms SHOULD be attempted.
4783
4784### Webpage-based Discovery
4785
4786Web pages MAY choose to advertise the location of a related xRegistry
4787server by including a `<link>` element in the page's `<head>` section.
4788The format of the element MUST adhere to:
4789
4790```yaml
4791<link rel="alternative" type="application/xregistry+json"
4792 title="STRING" href="URL"/>
4793```
4794
4795- Example:
4796 - ```yaml
4797 <link rel="alternative" type="application/xregistry+json"
4798 title="Our xRegistry server" href="https://xreg.example.com/"/>
4799 ```
4800
4801## Error Processing
4802
4803If an error occurs during the processing of a request, even if the error was
4804during the creation of the response (e.g. an invalid `inline` value was
4805provided), then an error MUST be generated and the entire request MUST be
4806undone.
4807
4808In general, when an error is generated, it SHOULD be sent back to the client.
4809However, this MAY not happen if the server determines there is a good reason
4810to not do so - such as due to security concerns.
4811
4812Each protocol binding specification will define how the error structure SHOULD
4813be returned back to clients.
4814
4815Each error definition consists of a set of fields as below:
4816
4817| Field Name | Description |
4818| --- | --- |
4819| Type | REQUIRED. MUST be a URI to the error definition/specification. |
4820| Code | REQUIRED. MUST be the HTTP response code and status text. |
4821| Title | REQUIRED. MUST be a short (non-empty) human-readable summary of the error. This SHOULD be sufficiently detailed for most users to determine what is the cause of the error. See the text below about substitution strings. |
4822| Detail | OPTIONAL. While "Title" conveys the critical error information, if additional details might be useful to users, such as hints as to how to fix the error, then this field SHOULD be used. |
4823| Subject | OPTIONAL. If present, MUST be a reference to the entity being processed when the error occurred. In the case of a Registry entity, it MUST be the XID of the entity. If no specific value is appropriate then this field MAY be excluded. MUST start with "/" when referencing an xRegistry entity or collection. |
4824| Args | OPTIONAL. A map of the substitution strings that were used when generating the "Title" text. |
4825| Instance | OPTIONAL. This is a non-empty string that can be used by servers to identify details related to the request/error processing. For example, a request or transaction ID of the request that generated the error. This information is not meant to be useful to clients directly, but can be provided to server administrators to help debugging if necessary. This specification places no restriction on the format of this value. |
4826| Source | OPTIONAL. A non-empty string representing the component that raised the error. Similar to "Instance", this is not meant to be used by clients, rather it is for debugging purposes. |
4827
4828The definition of each error's "Title" field MAY include substitutable
4829placeholders that allows for situational specific data to be included. Each
4830placeholder will be denoted as `<...>` in the "Title" text, where "..." MUST
4831be of the form `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, no longer than 63 characters, and
4832used as the key in the "Args" map. At runtime, each placeholder MUST be
4833replaced with the appropriate value from "Args", and "Args" (if non-empty)
4834MUST appear in the error structure returned to the client. As an optimization,
4835if "<subject>" is used then it MUST NOT be included "Args" as it MUST already
4836appear as a stand-alone field in the error structure.
4837
4838HTTP response codes and status text are defined in the [HTTP
4839Semantics](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#name-status-codes)
4840specification.
4841
4842The "Type", "Code", and "Subject" values MUST be as specified in error's
4843specification. The "Title" field MAY be modified as needed based on
4844the context in which the implementation is running. This includes being
4845specified in a language other than English, however it MUST still include the
4846same substitution values (possibly in a different order).
4847
4848In most user-facing scenarios, clients will only need to see the "Title" and
4849"Detail" fields. The other fields are provided for either administrative
4850purposes or to help enable 3rd party tooling.
4851
4852Most of the error conditions mentioned in this specification will include a
4853reference to one of the errors listed in this section. While it is RECOMMENDED
4854that implementations use those errors (for consistency), they MAY choose to use
4855a more appropriate one. Implementations MAY define additional extension
4856fields, as well as new error definitions. For new errors, it is RECOMMENDED
4857that the "Subject" value appears within the "Title" field, when appropriate.
4858
4859While not a requirement, it is RECOMMENDED that custom errors adhere to the
4860following rules for consistency:
4861- Make `Title` and `Detail` text complete sentences that start with a capital
4862 letter and end with a period.
4863- Include `<subject>` in `Title` so that end users only need to examine the
4864 `Title` to know what went wrong and which entity was being processed.
4865- Avoid using The terms `Group`, `Groups`, `Resources` and `Resource` when
4866 possible. Instead use the appropriate "singular" or "plural" type name for
4867 the entity in question. End users will likely not know what "Groups" or
4868 "Resources" are if they only work with the model defined entities.
4869- Use "Arg" names that are short descriptions of the value of the arg.
4870- Use `error_detail` as the "Arg" name for substitution text that provides
4871 more details about the error beyond the generic text provided by the
4872 error definition itself.
4873- When possible, try to differentiate names of entities from their surrounding
4874 text by using quotes, parentheses or a colon (":") separator to avoid cases
4875 where the name could be misinterpreted as a normal English word.
4876
4877**Examples:**
4878
4879An error serialized per the [HTTP binding specification](./http.md):
4880
4881```yaml
4882HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
4883Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
4884
4885{
4886 "type": "https://github.com/xregistry/spec/blob/main/core/spec.md#bad_flag",
4887 "title": "The specified flag (collections) is not allowed in this context: /schemagroups.",
4888 "subject": "/schemagroups",
4889 "args": {
4890 "flag": "collections"
4891 },
4892 "detail": "?collections is only allow on the Registry or Group instance level.",
4893 "instance": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
4894 "source": "parser:4123#d3beeeb5b0f"
4895}
4896```
4897
4898The following list of protocol-independent errors are defined:
4899
4900<!-- start-err-def -->
